title: Senior GenAI Solution Engineer (all genders)
description:
What you can expect from us We are a technical, implementation-oriented spin-off of a global management consultancy. Our clients are primarily DAX and Fortune Global 500 companies, which we advise on issues in the areas of analytics, big data and machine learning. Within the group, we take on the development of individual and data-driven solutions in order to transform our clients into AI-powered companies. We offer an international working environment with agile teams and creative startup methods as well as above-average remuneration and numerous additional benefits. With our offices in Hamburg, Munich and Düsseldorf and our hub locations in all other major German cities (Berlin, Frankfurt and Stuttgart), we ensure that all colleagues are integrated into our team of experts across Germany.

Your role as a Senior GenAI Solution Engineer: 

- End-to-End Development: You drive AI solutions across the full lifecycle - from rapid prototyping and proof-of-concept to deployment in scalable, highly available production environments.
- AI Services Engineering: You build robust backend services in Python that seamlessly integrate state-of-the-art LLMs and perform reliably under production load.
- Autonomous Agent Architecture: You design and implement intelligent agent systems that automate real-world workflows through tool calling and memory management, operating safely within defined guardrails.
- Agentic SDLC: You integrate AI agents into the development lifecycle - from AI-assisted coding and code reviews to automated testing and intelligent documentation - enhancing efficiency across the entire software development process through agentic tools.
- Ensuring Software Excellence: You take ownership of code quality by applying clean architecture principles, implementing automated testing, and establishing efficient CI/CD pipelines to ensure smooth and reliable deployments.
- Evaluation & Monitoring: You implement frameworks to measure the performance of GenAI solutions (e.g., accuracy, latency, cost) and ensure continuous optimization.
- Consulting: You work directly with clients - facilitating workshops and acting as a sparring partner for business and management stakeholders. You translate complex AI concepts into tangible business impact and co-create the right solutions.
- Technology Sparring: You assess technical feasibility and advise stakeholders on how to turn innovative ideas into sustainable, production-ready products.

Who you are - Excellent Python Skills (Production-Ready): You have strong expertise in API development (e.g., FastAPI, Pydantic), containerization (Docker), testing (unit and integration), as well as Git and CI/CD - well beyond notebook-based scripting.
- Rapid Prototyping: Ability to quickly build and visualize demos and proof-of-concepts.
- Strong Architectural Understanding: You apply SOLID principles, Clean Architecture, dependency injection, and async/concurrency patterns in a structured way, and leverage ORMs (e.g., SQLAlchemy) for clean and efficient database interactions.
- Hands-on Experience with Multimodal LLM APIs: Proficient in working with leading models (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) and cloud platforms (e.g., Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock).
- Advanced GenAI Engineering: Strong command of prompt engineering, structured outputs (JSON), and tool/function calling.
- RAG Expertise (End-to-End): Experience in building full pipelines - from embeddings and vector databases (e.g., pgvector) to advanced retrieval, re-ranking, and evaluation.
- Agent Development: Experience in designing and orchestrating autonomous systems (e.g., with Pydantic AI), including memory management and guardrails.
- Consulting Skills: Experience working directly with clients. You are able to facilitate workshops, present results, and confidently navigate complex stakeholder environments.
- Languages: Fluent in German (C1), with professional proficiency in English.
- Education: Completed degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, Data Science, Information Systems, or a comparable field (Bachelor’s degree or higher).
- Willingness to travel: You are willing to work on-site at the client’s premises on a regular basis

Who we are - Shape the future with (Gen)AI by working on diverse and impactful projects at the intersection of strategy, technology, and business.
- Work flexibly in a way that suits your life – with hybrid working models, flexible working hours, and the option to work from home.
- Enjoy an open, collaborative culture with flat hierarchies, an international team, and colleagues who are always willing to share their knowledge and support one another.
- A Great Place to Grow: Benefit from tailored learning opportunities, individualized career paths, and dedicated support for your professional and personal development.
- Be part of a strong international network of more than 1,300 colleagues and enjoy regular cross-office and international company events.
- Maintain a healthy work-life balance with flexible working models and, where appropriate, the opportunity to take a sabbatical.
- Take advantage of our Company Bike program and a subsidized EGYM Wellpass membership to support your health and wellbeing.
- Work from modern, centrally located offices in Hamburg, Munich, and Düsseldorf, as well as flexible hub locations across Germany's major cities.
- Enjoy complimentary drinks, fresh fruit, snacks, premium coffee – and, if you like, an after-work beer with your colleagues.
- Thrive in an environment built on trust, ownership, and continuous growth, where your ideas are valued regardless of your role or level of seniority

You ensure that our clients’ operational requirements define the framework for the solution. To achieve this, you define functional objectives together with the client, set priorities and steer internal IT, external SAP consultants and other service providers so that robust, practical and sustainable solutions are delivered.

You act as the central interface between Logistics, IT and implementation partners and represent our clients’ business interests clearly and consistently.

Your Responsibilities 

- You are responsible for the overall functional management of SAP EWM projects for our clients, including implementation, roll-out, optimization and, where applicable, migration from SAP WM to SAP EWM, from a Logistics / Supply Chain perspective.

- You coordinate and lead functional key users, process owners and, where applicable, internal EWM experts on the client side and support the development of a strong and reliable business team around EWM.

Who you are You combine strong logistics and process expertise with a good understanding of SAP EWM and the ability to translate business requirements into robust, practical solutions. You are comfortable navigating complex project and decision-making environments, manage different stakeholders with clarity and commitment, and challenge existing approaches with confidence. At the same time, you are comfortable working in a consulting environment and take ownership in demanding client projects.

In addition, you bring the following: 

- At least 5 years of experience in management consulting or in relevant industry roles with a focus on Logistics, Intralogistics or Supply Chain, ideally with responsibility for warehouse, distribution or production logistics.
- A university degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering or a comparable qualification.

- Proven expertise in requirements management, process design, test management, change management and stakeholder management.
- Experience in managing external SAP implementation partners and interdisciplinary teams, as well as the ability to provide clear functional leadership to IT teams and consultants.
- A structured, solution-oriented and dependable way of working, combined with assertiveness, diplomatic skills and a hands-on mindset.
- Very good German and good English skills, both written and spoken.

title: Account Executive – Full-Cycle, New Business (m/f/d)
description:
THE JOB Reading this to the end is worth it. 

The Company: Why mute-labs? 

mute-labs is the EU market leader in acoustic phone booths, with more than 20,000 cabins sold and counting. We are self-funded, profitable since day one, and have no investors to answer to and no exit to chase. What we do have is a steep growth curve in revenue, a product made in Germany, and a genuine mission: giving the modern office some quiet back. 

We have built a strong direct and dealer business on the back of inbound demand and word of mouth. What we have not built yet is a real outbound engine for winning bigger accounts on purpose, from ambitious growth companies to household names like Volkswagen, adidas, IKEA, Red Bull, or Axel Springer, who already trust us today. That gap is this role, and how far into that world you grow is largely up to you. 

Outbound is not a new idea for us. We have piloted it in smaller pockets already, testing signal-based outreach and structured sequences with real results. What has been missing is someone to own this as a dedicated motion for bigger accounts rather than a side project squeezed in between other things. That is why we are building this out as a new department and you’d be joining a small, yet focussed team as one of the first hires. 

The Role: Build the Pipeline AND the Channel 

This is a founding position. You are not stepping into an existing sales org with a quota handed down from three reps before you. You are the first one in the building. What you build, and how you build it, is largely up to you and your team, and you can grow the size and ambition of your target accounts as you find your footing. 

- Green Field, Full Ownership: Build your own pipeline from scratch. There is no inherited book of business and no recycled leads. The customer base you build is yours, and so is the revenue you generate from it. 

- Your Stack, Your Sequences: Clay, Reply.io, LinkedIn Premium, and Aircall are all at your disposal. You design your own outreach sequences, run your own cold calling campaigns, and decide how the machine works. Nobody hands you a script. 

- Segment Strategy, Together: You understand the market as well as anyone. Rather than being handed a target list from above, you and your manager will decide together which segments and account types are worth focusing on. 

- Comp That Rewards More Than the First Deal: An uncapped bonus with a kicker for overperformance. Returning customers you bring in keep feeding your comp over time, not just the initial close. Landing an account well is worth more than landing it once. 

- A Brand That Opens Doors: You are not cold-calling on behalf of an unknown startup. mute-labs is an established, well-regarded market leader with a reference list that already includes some of the biggest names in German and European business. That credibility is yours to use from day one. 

- A seasoned team to back you up: Your manager has built and run outbound and enterprise sales hands-on, from cold pipeline to six-figure closes, and will work closely with you from day one, coaching, supporting, and training wherever it's actually needed rather than just checking in on numbers. 

Is This You? 

- The Go-Getter: You do not wait to be told what to do next. You get on your feet quickly, figure out the shape of the problem, and start moving before anyone has to push you. 

- Sales Experience: You have carried a full sales cycle before, from first contact to signed contract, and know how to keep a deal moving without needing someone else to close it for you. You do not need to have sold into large enterprises already, that is something you will grow into here. 

- Stakeholder Management: You know how to work a deal with more than one person in the room, decision-makers, influencers, and budget holders, and you can keep several of those relationships moving in parallel without losing the thread. 

- Comfortable with Ambiguity: There is no existing playbook to inherit here. You will help write it. If you need every process defined for you before you can start, this is not the role. 

- Fluent in German and English: Most of your target accounts are DACH-based, though the reference list extends across the EU. Strong German is expected; English is the internal working language. 

Our Hiring Process 

We keep this fast and honest, on both sides. 

- The Spark: A short intro call with our People team to check for basic fit. 

- The deepdive: A conversation with your future manager Patrick about your experience, how you build your pipeline and how you close. Here you’ll also meet the rest of the team. 

- The Live Action: A live discovery or negotiation role-play based on a realistic enterprise scenario. No prep deck, just show us how you actually work a deal. 

- The Vision: A final conversation with Leah, Head of Sales as well as Franziskus, Managing Director, on the strategic mandate behind this role and where it can go from here. 

ABOUT US mute-labs exists to make quiet a normal part of the modern workplace. A few things that set us apart: 

- We are "no tech" : we build and sell real hardware, sound-insulated phone and meeting booths that companies actually need. 

- We have no investors , and we are not looking for any. We have been profitable since day one. 

- We are on a steep growth curve , measured in revenue and profit, not headcount for its own sake. 

- We are not building toward an exit . We are building a company meant to last for generations. 

Skip the Queue Told you it was worth reading to the end. 

We are looking for someone with a go-getter attitude who does not wait around for permission. So here is your first test: don't apply through the form. Cold call your future manager, Patrick, directly. 

+49 15888 279908 

If you get through and make your case, you've already shown us more than any CV could.

title: SAP Account Executive (m/w/d)
description:
Deine Aufgaben Du weißt, dass du zu den Besten gehörst.  Dein Umfeld weiß es auch.  Aber deine aktuelle Rolle gibt dir nicht mehr den Raum, den du verdienst.   Du hast in den letzten Jahren Deals geschlossen, die andere für unmöglich hielten. Du kennst das SAP-Ökosystem nicht aus Präsentationen – sondern aus echten Co-Sell-Gesprächen, aus Partnerverhandlungen, aus Abschlüssen, die du persönlich über die Linie gebracht hast.  Jetzt fragst du dich: Gibt es eine Rolle, die meinem Anspruch wirklich gerecht wird?   Die gibt es. Und du liest sie gerade. 

Die Rolle 

 Dies ist eine reine New-Business-Position mit klarer strategischer Bedeutung für Implicos Wachstum in SAP-zentrierten Prozessindustrien. Du verantwortest die Gewinnung neuer Kundenlogos in den Segmenten Landwirtschaft, Bergbau, Chemie sowie Zement und Baustoffe – in enger Co-Sell-Partnerschaft mit SAP Account Teams und Industry Business Units.  Du bewegst dich in einem Umfeld, in dem Vertrauen, Substanz und Marktkenntnisse entscheiden – nicht Lautstärke. 

Deine Verantwortung 
- Vollständige Quota-Verantwortung für neues ARR aus Prozessindustrie-Kunden
- Identifikation und Qualifizierung von Opportunities aus der SAP-ADRM-Pipeline sowie dem eigenen Netzwerk
- Aufbau und Pflege belastbarer Co-Sell-Beziehungen mit SAP SCM Sales Reps und IBU-Kontakten
- Steuerung komplexer Sales-Zyklen von 3–9 Monaten mit mehreren Entscheidungsträgern auf IT-, Operations- und C-Level-Ebene
- Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Solution Architects für technische Deep Dives und Proof-of-Value-Definitionen
- Akkurate Pipeline-Führung im CRM sowie strukturiertes Forecasting
- Kontinuierliche Rückmeldung von Markt- und Wettbewerbsinformationen an Product- und GTM-Teams

Dein Profil Was wir voraussetzen: 
- Mindestens 5 Jahre B2B-Softwarevertrieb, davon mindestens 3 Jahre im SAP-Umfeld oder im strukturierten Co-Sell mit SAP
- Nachweisliche Hunter-Bilanz: nachhaltig neue Kundenbeziehungen aufgebaut und abgeschlossen – nicht primär im Bestandsgeschäft
- Tiefes Verständnis der SAP Channel- und Co-Sell-Mechanismen: Partnerdeals, RISE/GROW-Pipeline, SAP-Partnerökosystem
- Erfahrung in der Steuerung von Multi-Stakeholder-Prozessen auf Entscheiderebene
- Souveränes Auftreten auf C-Level – verbindlich, präzise, auf Augenhöhe
- Ausgeprägte Eigenständigkeit in einem frühen, sich entwickelnden Go-to-Market-Setup
- Verhandlungssichere Kenntnisse in Deutsch und Englisch
Was dich zusätzlich auszeichnet: 
- Branchenwissen in Landwirtschaft, Bergbau, Chemie oder Zement/Baustoffe
- Bestehendes Netzwerk in der SAP SCM- oder Logistik-IBU-Community
- Erfahrung im Vertrieb von SAP-Add-ons oder SolEx-Produkten
- Vertrautheit mit Supply-Chain-Execution-, TM- oder Bulk-Logistik-Prozessen

Was du bei uns findest 
- Eine strategisch bedeutsame Rolle mit direktem Einfluss auf das Unternehmenswachstum
- Klare Ziele, volle Autonomie in der Ausführung – kein Mikromanagement
- Ungedeckeltes Vergütungsmodell – dein Upside spiegelt deinen Beitrag
- Direkter Zugang zum SAP-Ökosystem und enge Zusammenarbeit mit erfahrenen Solution Architects
- Ein Umfeld, das Seniorität respektiert und Eigenverantwortung erwartet
Du gestaltest – nicht nur mit. Du gestaltest, wie es wird. 

 Implico ist kein fertig gebautes Konstrukt, das auf einen weiteren Vertriebsmitarbeiter wartet. Diese Rolle ist eine der ersten ihrer Art – du definierst mit, wie wir in den Prozessindustrien wahrgenommen werden, wie wir co-sellen, wie wir skalieren. Was du heute aufbaust, bleibt. Dein Fingerabdruck ist sichtbar – in der Kundenbasis, in der Marktpositionierung, in der Art, wie das Team in zwei Jahren arbeitet. Das ist kein Job. Das ist ein Gestaltungsauftrag.

Das Team – kein Versprechen, sondern eine Einladung. 

 "Tolles Team" steht in jeder Stellenanzeige. Das überspringst du längst. Deshalb sagen wir es anders: Schau dir an, mit wem du zusammenarbeiten würdest.  Mark, Maurice, Anna, Thales, Selina und mehr. Menschen, die nicht wegen des Titels hier sind. Die morgens mit echtem Interesse an ihre Arbeit gehen. Die füreinander einspringen, ohne dass jemand fragen muss. Die über ihre Themen sprechen, als wären es ihre eigenen Projekte – weil sie es sind. Keine perfekte Hochglanz-Kultur. Aber eine, in der Leidenschaft und Haltung mehr zählen als Hierarchie.  Ob das zu dir passt? Das findest du nur heraus, wenn du das Gespräch suchst.

Der nächste Schritt 

 Wenn du in den letzten Jahren bewiesen hast, dass du im SAP-Umfeld neue Märkte erschließt und Abschlüsse bringst dann freuen wir uns auf ein erstes, offenes Gespräch.  Kein langes Anschreiben. Zeig uns deinen Track Record – der Rest ergibt sich.

title: Working Student (m/f/d)​Indexing Platform
description:
Company Description Since its creation in 2007 in the financial city of Frankfurt am Main, Solactive AG has grown to one of the key players in the indexing space. The German multi-asset index provider focusses on tailor-made indices, offering to its clients a faster service, with greater flexibility and at a reasonable cost. Solactive AG and its subsidiaries have become one of the fastest growing index providers over the past few years and support the leading investment banks and asset managers across the globe. We have gained global recognition for our role in the Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) industry, where we rank among the top providers worldwide for underlying indices. We also excel in diverse areas such as Structured Products and investment mandates, showcasing the wide range of our capabilities. The impact and value we bring to the market is palpable, but also in the reputation we have proudly built by being close to our customers, solidifying Solactive AG as a trusted and reliable ally in the ever-evolving global financial landscape.

Job Overview Solactive's Aggregate team owns the intraday calculation of our indices: consuming live price streams, applying calculation logic across a wide range of indices, and producing a continuous output stream of index ticks throughout the trading day. The core platform is built in Java and engineered around throughput, latency, and correctness under concurrency, while custom business integrations are built in Python. As a Working Student you join a small team and contribute real, production-bound code to both, working alongside senior engineers who review your work and coach you.

Your Tasks - Implement well-scoped features and fixes in the Java calculation platform, such as improvements to calculation components, price stream consumption, or index tick production
- Write unit, integration, and performance tests, including tests for concurrent code paths where ordering and timing matter
- Help investigate correctness or performance issues: reproduce them, narrow them down, and propose fixes with senior guidance
- Build and maintain Python integrations for business teams: connectors to the calculation platform, output adapters, validation checks, and small operational tools
- Contribute to monitoring and developer tooling that makes calculation behaviour observable and easier to reason about
- Take part in design and code reviews, ask questions, and document what you learn so the next person can pick it up faster

Your Profile - Enrolled student in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field
- Strong Java fundamentals: object-oriented design, collections, generics, and comfort reading and writing idiomatic modern Java
- Solid grounding in core computer science: data structures, algorithms, and complexity, and in particular a working understanding of multithreading and concurrency (threads, synchronisation, memory visibility, races and deadlocks)
- Openness to Python: no prior experience needed, but willingness to pick it up for integration and tooling work alongside Java
- Familiarity with Git, the command line, and a testing mindset; interest in measuring performance rather than guessing at it
- Ability to work independently on a scoped task, ask for help early when stuck, and communicate clearly in writing
- Available for 15–20 hours per week during the semester, more during semester breaks
- Interest in financial markets, market data, or index calculation is welcome but not required

Our Offer - Be part of the Solactive family an international FinTech environment with flat hierarchies, real ownership, and strong growth opportunities.
- Enjoy attractive benefits such as team events, Corporate Benefits access, a modern ergonomic office,free beverages and fruit.
- Work on a real, high-impact production platform and contribute to architectural improvements not just feature tickets.
- Gain hands-on experience with Java microservices, build systems, and dependency governance while collaborating with experienced engineers.
- Build practical backend engineering skills that directly support your long-term career development.

title: Talent Acquisition Executive - THG Nutrition | Myprotein
description:

Our portfolio of leading retailers and brands such as LOOKFANTASTIC, Myprotein, ESPA, Perricone MD, and Cult Beauty form our two core businesses: THG Beauty and THG Nutrition.

With us, you’ll go further, faster. What are you waiting for?

Division: Nutrition 

Brand: Myprotein

Your work will span the full hiring process: shaping briefs, finding and engaging candidates, managing interviews, and helping teams make confident hiring decisions.

Your focus will be on Head Office and commercial vacancies. Menlo Security is building MARS for Agents (Menlo Agent Runtime Security), our product line for securing autonomous and hybrid AI agents. Success Metrics / KPIs 

- Roadmap delivery: committed roadmap items for the owned surfaces shipped within the target release window.

- Requirements quality: Reduction in mid-sprint requirement clarifications and rework attributable to ambiguous PRDs or acceptance criteria, measured via engineering feedback each quarter.

- Enablement coverage: 100% of shipped capabilities in the owned area have current capability documentation and a delivered briefing to support and solutions engineering at or before release.

- Adoption of shipped capability: Customer adoption or usage of newly released capabilities against a target set at launch, tracked for 90 days post-release.

- Competitive influence: At least one documented roadmap or positioning decision per quarter, traceable to a published competitive finding.

What You'll Do 

- Own inbound product direction for your area. Research emerging agentic AI capabilities, attacker techniques, and adjacent standards (MCP, A2A, OWASP agentic-security guidance, agent identity frameworks) to determine what MARS for Agents should build next across the agent registry, Claude integration, Microsoft Copilot integration, MCP Server, MCP Proxy, and LLM proxy.

- Turn signal into engineering-ready requirements. Translate market, customer, and competitive input into clear PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria — using LLM-based tools to synthesize call notes, support tickets, standards documents, and usage data into prioritization insight, while retaining full accountability for the judgment calls and the accuracy of what you write.

- Own and groom the backlog. Make day-to-day prioritization calls across your surfaces within the strategic guardrails set by the Head of Product, and partner directly with engineering through the full build cycle: refinement, in-sprint questions, review, and release.

Use AI coding assistants, MCP clients, and agent runtimes hands-on to prototype and stress-test proposed behavior — so requirements are grounded in how agents actually behave, not just how they are documented to behave. Define success metrics for what you ship and track them post-release.

Brief technical support and solutions engineering on new and existing capabilities, and maintain current capability documentation for your area that clearly separates documented and shipping facts from planned work and open questions, so the field never over-promises. - Run competitive analysis that changes decisions. Continuously track competitors relevant to MARS for Agents — network/SSE-SASE incumbents (Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler, Cloudflare, Netskope), agent-identity and IAM players (Okta, CyberArk), MCP gateway vendors, and emerging agent-security pure-plays — and maintain a clear point of view on where MARS leads, where it currently trails, and what capabilities are commoditizing. Functional Competencies 

Required: 

- 6–10+ years of product management or product owner experience, ideally in B2B SaaS, enterprise infrastructure, or security software, including a track record of owning a complex, technical product area end to end.

- Demonstrated ability to write clear, engineering-ready requirements (PRDs, user stories, acceptance criteria) and to own a backlog end to end for a technically complex product surface.

This role receives strategic direction rather than daily instruction, and the person in it should be able to take a goal and drive it through research, requirements, engineering partnership, and launch across multiple related surfaces at once — with the support of a collaborative product and engineering team.

- Comfort operating at high velocity. Our engineering organization runs agile at a fast cadence, and this role also helps bring the process and rigor needed to make the product scalable, so both muscles matter.

- Real cybersecurity background, with working familiarity in areas such as identity and access management, proxy and gateway architectures (forward proxy, reverse proxy, secure web gateway / SSE / SASE), and content or traffic inspection. Deep specialization in every area is not required, but enough fluency to engage credibly with engineering and with technical customers is.

Preferred / Nice to Have:

- Prior product ownership of an identity or registry system, a proxy or gateway product, or an API/integration platform.

- Direct experience with MCP, LLM/agent tool-calling architectures, or building integrations with Claude or other frontier model providers.

- Familiarity with OWASP frameworks, including emerging OWASP guidance for agentic AI security.

- Experience directly supporting a technical sales motion — SE enablement, competitive battlecards, customer discovery calls.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

title: Senior Optical Packaging & Assembly Engineer
description:
PsiQuantum’s mission is to build the first useful quantum computers—machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems. 

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries. 

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry—including partners like GlobalFoundries—we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don’t feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure. 

In 2024, PsiQuantum announced government-funded projects to support the build-out of our first utility-scale quantum computers in Brisbane, Australia, and Chicago, Illinois. These initiatives reflect a growing recognition that quantum computing will be strategically and economically defining—and that now is the time to scale. 

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies—including Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical—to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact. 

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift—and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we have a clear path to make it real. 

Come join us. 

Job Summary: 

The Senior Optical Packaging Engineer is responsible for developing & implementing high-performance, robust & scalable opto-electronic packaging workflows for a variety of chip-based photonic integrated circuits. This work will be carried out in PsiQuantum’s UK R&D facility located in Daresbury Lab.

Responsibilities: 

- Develop an optical package and fibre-to-chip alignment scheme that allows for high alignment accuracy and scalable assembly.

- Help develop packaging prototypes & scalable fibre-to-chip packaging flows and processes.

- Review packaging design BOMs, work with supply chain on procuring parts needed for assembly.

- Work with our internal packaging team and external vendors on transferring & scaling packaging designs and processes based on successful prototypes.

- Work with external vendors and suppliers to source required materials and provide feedback on evolving requirements. 

- Working with external partners to develop advanced opto-electronic packaging solutions.

Experience/Qualifications: 

- Master’s Degree or above in Optical Engineering, Physics or equivalent.

- 3+ years of experience working on PIC packaging design & qualification.

- 5+ years of experience working with optical fibers, optical measurements.

- 3+ years of experience working on FAU / optical connector to chip attachment.

- Experience with optical data analysis.

title: Campaign Manager
description:
📈 Who We Are: 

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair. 

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

The Role 

We run multi-channel brand campaigns: social, content, video, out-of-home, events and road shows, often all at once. We've got plenty of ideas and a growing calendar. What we're missing is someone who owns delivery from the first brief to the final asset, across every channel. This is a hands-on generalist role. 

Campaign ideas can come from the wider team (or yourself!), but you'll make it happen: the plan, the timeline, the budget, the agency or freelancer, the channel mix, the logistics when a campaign goes offline, and sometimes even copy or campaign set up. You organise and you do. You’re the connect point between Brand & Credibility and other teams, internal and external. 

You'll work day to day with the Brand and Credibility team, our product marketers, and across tem's other teams as campaigns touch them. You will:

- Own campaigns from brief to delivery across owned and offline channels, on brand, on time, on budget.

- Plan and run events and support road shows.

- Find, brief and manage agencies and freelancers: creative, media, production, experiential.

- Keep multiple projects moving at once across teams that don't report to you.

- Embed AI workflows or tooling to maximize efficiency and effectiveness in our service

Responsibilities 

Campaign delivery

- Build briefs, timelines and budget plans, then drive execution to completion.

- Keep deliverables aligned across channels and accurate, working with product marketing to check every claim.

- Spot and act on comms opportunities around key brand moments.

- Align the Brand and Credibility campaign calendar with the rest of the business needs

- Run a short post-campaign review each time so the next one is sharper.

Events and offline

- Own roadshow support, customer events and out-of-home from planning through to the day itself, including the logistics.

- Travel to events roughly once a month (a day or two, UK).

- Manage merch and swag: design, ordering, distribution.

- Support in the branding needs around our bi-annual internal company-wide event, temfest

Agencies and freelancers

- Source and manage external partners, own the brief and artwork through to delivery, and hold them to time and budget.

- Coordinate freelancer-led paid tests when we run them. You don't need to run paid yourself (but huge plus if you can).

Requirements 

Must haves

- 2-4 years in a marketing, agency or creative production role where you delivered multi-channel campaigns or events end to end.

- You've managed budgets and kept projects on time and on spec, including at least one that got messy.

- You've sourced, briefed and managed external partners: agencies, freelancers, suppliers.

- Comfortable with ambiguity: you can take a one-line brief and turn it into a plan, then adjust when priorities shift.

- You use AI tools daily to plan, write, analyse faster, and empower others.

Bonus points

- Agency background (account management, project management, creative ops, production).

- B2B or B2B tech experience, and a view on which B2B brands are doing it well and why.

- You've set up basic paid social or search campaigns yourself.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

title: GRC Security Specialist
description:
About Abound 

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.

And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.

Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

The role 

We are formalising our security assurance function. We have technical controls and the engineering culture; what we need now is the governance layer that proves it - to our auditors, to our funders, and to our regulator.

You will be the delivery engine behind that. You will own the recurring assurance cycle end to end, run our third-party security programme, and be the person who turns evidence into something a due diligence team or a certification auditor can be satisfied by.

You will be responsible for building controls, gathering evidence, and challenging suppliers.

What you will own: 

1. Third-party security assurance 

- Run security due diligence on new suppliers, maintain initial questionnaire to risk sign-off, working with Procurement and Legal on security and data protection schedules.

- Maintain a supplier tiering model based on criticality and run the periodic re-assessment cycle for tiered suppliers: certification expiry, subprocessor changes, breach notifications, SLA performance.

- Maintain the supplier and outsourcing registers, including preparation for the FCA's material third party register under PS26/2 (rules in force 18 March 2027).

- Track concentration risk and exit plans for critical suppliers.

2. Inbound due diligence and customer assurance 

- Own our response to security due diligence from funders, banking partners, institutional investors, commercial partners and prospects.

- Build and maintain a reusable trust pack: answer library, security whitepaper, current certifications, pen test attestations, standard questionnaire pre-fills (SIG, CAIQ).

- Turn a 40-hour bespoke questionnaire response into a 4-hour one.

3. The assurance calendar 

- Maintain the annual calendar of security activities and make sure each one happens, produces evidence, and closes its actions: penetration tests, access reviews, disaster recovery tests, tabletop exercises, policy reviews, supplier re-assessments, awareness training.

- Coordinate external penetration tests: scoping, vendor selection, scheduling, findings triage, remediation tracking, retest.

- Facilitate tabletop exercises, including scenario design and post-exercise action tracking.

4. Risk and control administration 

- Maintain the information security risk register: run the assessment cycle, record treatment plans with named owners and dates, chase closure.

- Administer the policy exception and risk acceptance process, ensuring every exception is owned, time-bound and reviewed on expiry.

- Perform first-line control testing: sample-test where key controls operate as designed and retain the evidence.

- Produce security MI for the Head of Security to take to ExCo and the Risk Committee.

5. Vulnerability and findings management 

- Consolidate findings across sources — EDR, cloud security posture, SAST/DAST/SCA, secrets scanning, penetration tests — into a single view with agreed severity definitions and remediation SLAs.

- Triage, route and chase remediation with engineering teams; escalate ageing findings.

- Own the reporting on remediation performance.

6. Security awareness 

- Run the awareness programme: induction, annual refresher, phishing simulation, role-based training for engineers, completion tracking.

- Coordinate pre-employment screening with People.

What you will contribute to: 

- The ISO 27001 ISMS , which we are building towards certification. You will draft and maintain control documentation, populate the Statement of Applicability, gather evidence, coordinate the internal audit programme and be a primary point of contact for our external auditor. The Head of Security owns the framework, scope, and risk appetite.

- Policies and standards: you will draft, review and shepherd policies through approval, and track the review cycle.

- Incident response: you will maintain the IR plan and playbooks, facilitate post-incident reviews, track remediation actions, and support regulatory notification (ICO personal data breach reporting within 72 hours; FCA notification under Principle 11 / SUP 15.3).

- Business continuity and DR: you will maintain the documentation and the testing evidence.

- Secure development: you will help embed security requirements into the SDLC and support threat modelling sessions.

- Data protection: you will support RoPA maintenance, DPIA completion and DSAR handling alongside Legal.

What success looks like: 

First 90 days: you know our supplier estate and have tiered it; the assurance calendar for the next 12 months is published and owned; inbound due diligence requests come to you and go out without the Head of Security rewriting them.

Six months: the trust pack exists and is being used; the risk register is live with owned treatment plans; ISO 27001 evidence collection is systematic rather than a scramble; the exception register exists.

Twelve months: supplier re-assessment runs on a cadence without prompting; the material third party register is ready ahead of the March 2027 deadline; MI to the Risk Committee is trusted.

Essential experience: 

- Three or more years in an information security assurance, GRC or security compliance role, at least some of it in a regulated financial services environment or another environment with real external audit pressure.

- Hands-on experience of ISO 27001, whether operating an ISMS or taking one through certification.

- Demonstrable experience running third-party or vendor security assessments, and of responding to inbound security due diligence.

- Comfortable reading technical findings — an EDR vulnerability report, a penetration test finding, a cloud misconfiguration — and forming your own view on severity and real-world exploitability rather than passing the vendor's rating through unchanged.

- Clear, concise written English. Much of this role is writing things that external parties will judge us on.

- The confidence to chase a busy engineer, challenge a supplier's assertion, and tell us when an answer is not good enough.

Desirable: 

- Experience of a cloud-native environment, ideally AWS.

- Experience of scaling a control framework as an organisation grows.

- Familiarity with UK operational resilience expectations (SYSC 15A) and outsourcing requirements (SYSC 8).

- Certifications such as CISM, CISA, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, CRISC or CCSP. We care more about what you have done than what you hold.

description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🐙 Kraken Generation Flex

The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing.

🚀 What you'll own

- Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

- Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team.

- Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.

- Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.

- Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers.

- Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.

- Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows.

- Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

- Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets.

- Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process.

- Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.

- Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation.

- Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control.

- Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation.

- Hardware and Networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support.

- Industrial Communication Protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus.

- CAD, Diagrams and Tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion.

- Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with the team.

- Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them.

- Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field - or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration.

- A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time.

- Travel: Willingness to travel to customers and sites although travel is very occasional. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote.

⭐️ Bonus points

- Wider knowledge of grid compliance (G99, G100, Grid Code) and where the Kraken system fits in.

- Experience with AWS IoT Greengrass or similar edge-deployment architectures.

- Familiarity with software/scripting and templating (e.g. Python, Rust, the Linux command line) and Git-based workflows.

- Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector (IEC 62443, NIS Regulations awareness).

- Exposure to wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks and TSO integrations.

🏡 Where you'll fit in: 
KrakenFlex is the flexibility arm of the Kraken group, built to put a big green dent in global carbon emissions by rewriting how electricity grids operate. We stabilize the grid and help renewables come online much faster by managing the second-by-second balance of clean power. Right now, our platform connects nearly one million assets worldwide, putting over 6GW of live load under our direct control.

Behind the scenes, that means handling massive technical scale: solving complex optimization problems in real time and processing 15 billion data readings a day from the latest green technologies, ensuring the grid stays reliable without relying on old fossil-fuel backup plants.

The next phase of our journey involves monumental growth. Currently operational across multiple countries, we are poised for further global expansion, scaling our asset base and tackling unique grid challenges in new territories. Our mission is to integrate an increasingly diverse array of green flexibility assets while ensuring our market-leading platform remains exceptionally stable and performant.

What is Optimisation in Flex? 
The Optimisation chapter is the mathematical and algorithmic engine of the KrakenFlex platform. While other chapters manage physical asset connectivity or ingest market signals, this domain is responsible for the intelligence that decides exactly what every asset should do, second by second, to maximise both grid stability and financial returns.

The teams within this chapter build and maintain the real-time dispatch engines, predictive forecasting models, and algorithmic solvers that handle massive multi-asset portfolios. This involves translating complex market rules, physical asset constraints (like battery degradation curves, state-of-charge limits, and ramp rates), and fluctuating price signals into optimised execution strategies.

The defining challenge for this chapter is scaling computational performance alongside our rapid asset growth. Running complex, multi-variable mathematical models in tight real-time windows requires immense efficiency. The core tension lies in balancing the demand from data science and quantitative engineering to introduce increasingly sophisticated models with the strict platform requirement for absolute reliability, low latency, and cost-effective cloud compute.

Ultimately, this chapter must move away from bespoke optimisation routines tailored to individual markets or asset types. Your goal is to architect a highly performant, modular optimisation core that uses standard abstract layers, allowing us to roll out new algorithms or expand into new global territories without rewriting the underlying engine.

The Flex platform is built on autonomous Chapters, which are collections of specialists focused on delivering a core service or business outcome, defined by the unchanging nature of the energy business (independent of technology, hardware, or regional differences). This role requires influencing beyond its formal remit, spotting cross-team patterns, clarifying ownership and decision-making, and driving initiatives to turn recurring issues into visible actions with owners, dates, and measures of success. Ultimately, they maintain the technical vision for their specific area, ensuring services are appropriately owned, maintained, and aligned with Flex's sustainable growth.

description:

Augur transforms legacy sensor systems into real-time operational intelligence. We help organisations act before threats escalate – not after damage is done. Everything we build is privacy-first by design.

Our platform connects to existing cameras and sensors to detect threats, retrace events, and surface real-time insights – all without replacing a single device. Augur helps teams reduce risk, cut costs, and grow revenue through better visibility, faster decisions, and fewer blind spots.

Our culture is built on a foundation of radical candor and mutual trust. We recognise that being an industry leader requires more than just building exceptional products – it requires empowering a team of exceptional people. Individually, we operate with high autonomy; collectively, we’re unified by a shared drive to achieve our mission through a commitment to excellence.

We're looking for a Robotics Engineer to join our growing technical team in London and take ownership of the integration of a new counter-UAS initiative.

This role sits at the intersection of robotics, machine learning and systems engineering, and you'll own the integration across all three. You'll prove out the concept, build the prototype, and take it into trials, working closely with product partners and other stakeholders along the way.

The role is highly interdisciplinary, so we're less concerned with ticking every box than with finding someone motivated, curious, and willing to learn. Across the project, you'll draw on areas such as:

- Machine learning and computer vision

- Sensors and camera modelling

- State estimation and sensor fusion

- Control theory

- Modelling and simulation

- Low-level programming and hardware/software integration

We don't expect you to be an expert in all of these. If you're strong in some and excited to grow into the rest, we'd like to hear from you. 

What We're Looking For 

- A degree in robotics, electrical engineering, computer science, mathematics or a related field - or another engineering background backed by hands-on hardware/software integration work.

- Strong programming skills in a low-level language (C, C++ or Rust), plus Python.

- A working understanding of modern computer vision, including object detection and tracking, and experience training, optimising, and deploying models for real-time or resource-constrained use.

- Hands-on experience with state estimation and sensor fusion - using techniques such as Kalman filtering and factor graphs to combine noisy sensor data into reliable estimates - and with the problems they underpin, such as SLAM.

- A solid grasp of sensors and how to model them: you understand how real sensors behave, particularly cameras, and can represent them with appropriate models (e.g. camera and distortion models).

- Self-directed initiative: you can take an unfamiliar problem, get up to speed through your own research, and clearly document and share your findings so others can build on them.

- Strong communication skills: you can explain technical work clearly and work effectively with external partners and suppliers.

Nice to Have 

- A working knowledge of control theory, particularly designing and tuning PID controllers for closed-loop systems.

- Experience developing and testing systems before committing to hardware, from numerical modelling through to 3D simulation.

- Familiarity with RF and RF-based sensing, including how RF sensors and sensor arrays work.

Accessibility and inclusivity 

At Augur, our culture is built on radical candor and mutual trust. To solve the complex, physical-world problems our customers face, we need a team that thinks differently. 

Whether you’re self-taught, have a non-traditional background, or are returning to the workforce, if you have the grit and the experience we’re looking for at Augur, we’d love to hear from you. 

We are committed to fostering a diverse workplace and ensuring an accessible hiring experience - please let us know if you require any accommodations during the interview process to help you do your best work.

The Finance Business Partner will be embedded within the Project Controllership Organization, acting as the finance owner for large, long-duration capital projects from initial commitment through to completion and transfer to operations. You will bring rigorous project and cost accounting to the delivery teams: owning capex and cost accounting for your projects, building and maintaining project cost structures, tracking budgets, commitments and actuals, reporting variances with insight, and ensuring each project is accounted for accurately under US GAAP and closed out cleanly at completion. This is a hands-on role that pairs technical accounting depth with genuine business partnering - you will sit alongside project directors, engineers and procurement, not apart from them.

What You Will Be Doing 

Project and capex accounting 

- Capex accounting: own end-to-end accounting for assigned capital projects, including construction in progress (CIP/AUC), capitalization assessments under US GAAP (ASC 360), componentization, capitalized interest where applicable (ASC 835-20), and transfer to fixed assets on completion with correct in-service dates and useful lives.

- Compute and equipment capex: own the accounting for high-value compute and network equipment (GPU fleets and associated infrastructure), including vendor purchase order and financing payment tracking, delivery acceptance and in-service dating, componentization and useful lives, residual value support, and lessor accounting for intra-group equipment leases (ASC 842).

- Cost accounting: maintain accurate, complete and well-classified project cost records - distinguishing capital from operating expenditure, applying the capitalization policy consistently, and ensuring costs land in the correct entity, project, site and cost category.

- Project costing: build and own project cost breakdown structures (WBS/cost codes) aligned to contracts, procurement packages and the accounting dimension framework; establish cost baselines and estimates-at-completion (EAC) and keep them current.

- Accruals and commitments: run monthly cost accruals from contractor applications for payment, certifications and goods receipts; maintain the committed cost position (POs, contracts, change orders) and reconcile committed, accrued and actual spend.

- Month-end close: deliver project close activities to the group timetable - CIP reconciliations, accrual journals, retention and milestone payment tracking, and balance sheet substantiation for project-related accounts.

Reporting, variance analysis and forecasting 

- Variance reporting: produce monthly project cost reports comparing actuals and EAC against budget and prior forecast; explain variances with root-cause commentary and work with project teams on corrective actions.

- Forecasting: partner with FP&A and Strategic Finance on capex cashflow forecasting, phasing of spend, and funding drawdown planning for your projects. Provide current capex phasing and estimate-at-completion data into Strategic Finance's monthly business plan refresh.

- Board and investor reporting: contribute project cost and progress data to board packs, lender/investor reporting and management information, ensuring one version of the truth between delivery and finance. Work within, and help build, the group project reporting framework.

- Balance sheet visibility: own the project-related balance sheet - CIP, retentions, VAT recoverable, prepayments and committed spend - and feed these positions into the group management balance sheet dashboard on an automated, near-real-time basis.

Project lifecycle and business partnering 

- Cradle to completion: support projects through their full lifecycle - business case and budget setting, contract award, execution, change management, practical completion, final account settlement, and financial close-out including release of retentions and accrual true-ups.

- Change control: evaluate the cost and accounting impact of scope changes, change orders and claims; ensure changes are approved, coded and forecast before costs are incurred.

- Business partnering: act as the trusted finance counterpart to project directors, construction managers, procurement and engineering; challenge constructively, translate financial data into decisions, and embed cost discipline in delivery teams.

- Contract and procurement support: work with procurement and legal on the financial aspects of construction and equipment contracts (payment mechanisms, milestones, retentions, bonds, liquidated damages) and ensure compliance with the Group Procurement Policy and PO controls.

Controls, policy and audit 

- Controls: operate and help design internal controls over project costs, capitalization and payments as part of the group's SOX 404 readiness program, including preparing clear documentation and audit evidence.

- Policy: apply and help refine group accounting policies (capitalization, PP&E, procurement) and prepare technical accounting analysis for project-specific matters, escalating judgmental issues with well-structured recommendations.

- Audit: act as the primary project-accounting contact for external audit on assigned projects, preparing schedules, reconciliations and supporting evidence.

- Anything else that makes sense: as an early hire in a fast-scaling finance function, contribute to systems implementation (ERP selection ongoing), process design, and whatever else is needed to build best-in-class project controllership.

What You Bring 

- Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA or equivalent) with strong post-qualification experience.

- Demonstrable experience of project accounting for large, long-term capital projects - for example data centers, energy, utilities, infrastructure, construction or industrial facilities - covering the full project lifecycle.

- Deep, practical knowledge of capex and cost accounting: CIP/AUC, capitalization criteria, componentization, accruals from contractor valuations, retentions, and asset transfer at completion.

- Experience building and managing project cost structures (WBS/cost coding), budgets, committed cost tracking and estimates-at-completion.

- Strong variance analysis and reporting skills, with the ability to explain cost movements clearly to non-finance stakeholders.

- Proven business partnering experience embedded with, or working closely alongside, project delivery teams.

title: Platform Engineer (10x Openings)
description:
About Volta 

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About The Role 

Volta builds and operates large scale GPU compute infrastructure for AI workloads. Our platform is Kubernetes-native, spans multiple regions, and delivers virtual machines, storage, and networking through a fully automated infrastructure stack built on custom Kubernetes operators.

We are building out several platform engineering teams that together own the full stack, from managed bare metal and IaaS through to higher-order platform services. Each team owns a different part of that stack: compute, networking, storage, the control plane and API layer, confidential computing, and the customer-facing surface. The area you work in depends on the team you join and your prior expertise, so no single engineer is expected to cover all of it.

Platform Engineers work at the intersection of infrastructure and software development. Across every team, you will translate three key inputs into durable platform capabilities: product roadmap requirements from the product team, operational learnings from the bring-up teams, and security guidance from the security engineering team. The output of this role is production platform code, not configuration, not runbooks.

What You Will Be Doing 

Common across every platform engineering team:

- Design and implement Kubernetes operators and controllers that manage the lifecycle of platform resources.

- Work closely with the product team to turn roadmap requirements into the platform capabilities that support them.

- Collaborate with the bring-up teams to identify operational pain points and turn them into scalable platform features.

- Integrate security guidance from the security engineering team into platform-level controls, and remediate findings at the platform layer.

- Treat observability as a platform concern: instrument services, define meaningful metrics, and build tooling that gives the team visibility into platform health.

- Own the services you build in production, including participation in an on-call rotation, incident response, and the follow-up work that closes structural gaps rather than only the immediate issue.

- Hold to clean interface and versioning practice on anything other teams or customers depend on, including disciplined handling of breaking changes.

- Participate in code review, technical design discussions, and cross-team collaboration in an Agile (Kanban or Scrum) environment.

Depending on your team and background, you will go deep in some of the following:

- Control plane and APIs: improve and extend the API layer between user-facing services and the underlying platform, with disciplined versioning and backward compatibility.

- Compute: build and operate the lifecycle of virtualized and bare metal compute resources.

- Storage: provisioning workflows, attachment reliability, performance tuning, and failure handling.

- Confidential computing: build and extend confidential computing capabilities across the stack, from secure bare metal and confidential VMs to Confidential Containers (CoCo).

- Customer-facing services: the platform surfaces customers interact with directly, including the APIs and interfaces through which they consume capacity, working alongside product and UX.

What You Bring 

- 3 to 5 years of software engineering experience, with a meaningful portion spent on infrastructure or platform systems.

- Strong backend or systems programming experience in a production environment. Our working languages are Python, Go, and Rust; we welcome strong engineers from other compiled or object-oriented languages (for example C++, C#, or Java) who are ready to work across our stack as it evolves.

- Solid understanding of Kubernetes internals: the control loop model, CRDs, controllers and operators, and reliable reconciliation logic.

- Comfortable working close to the infrastructure layer: Linux, networking fundamentals, and distributed systems behavior.

- Experience designing, building, and versioning production-grade APIs or service interfaces that other teams depend on, including disciplined handling of breaking changes and backward compatibility.

- Experience operating what you build: debugging production systems, and taking part in on-call or incident response.

- Strong engineering fundamentals: clean code, testing, version control, code review, and CI/CD practices.

Nice to Have (But Not Essential) 

None of these are required. Several map to specific teams, so strength in one or more helps us match you to the right one:

title: Lead Product Designer  (AEX)
description:
Lead Product Designer 

📍 Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH) 

💰 £70k-£90k (negotiable) 

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology.

We're now looking for a Lead Product Designer - the most senior individual contributor for design within a product domain. This is predominantly an IC role: you'll set the design bar for an entire domain through the quality of your own work, the patterns you contribute, and the way you raise the designers around you. We're flexible on this for the right person, if you've got management experience, or want to line-manage one or two designers alongside the IC work, let's talk.

We want someone who is tired of the "feature factory" grind, who is past needing to be told what's worth working on, and who is ready to set the design direction for a domain in one of the most exciting PropTech companies in the UK.

If you look at most UX job ads, you see a laundry list of requirements. We prefer to tell you how we actually operate so you can decide if this is the right environment for you.

- At Street Group, design is a strategic seat. Lead Product Designers drive roadmap conversations alongside their product and engineering counterparts, not respond to them.

- Our users rely on us to run their businesses, so they love talking to us. You can spin up a call and validate a prototype instantly. We don't guess; we ask.

- We move at pace, including on strategic work. Strategy isn't a separate, slower track here - we test it by shipping.

Here's what you can expect to be working on as an L6 Lead Product Designer at Street Group 

- Own the design vision and execution for a product domain. Translate strategic direction into the most ambiguous, cross-cutting, or strategically important pieces of design work.

- Set the craft bar through your own output. The work you ship is the reference point for what good looks like in your area.

- Own the cross-cutting design problems: patterns across multiple features, flows across multiple surfaces, the coherence of the domain's experience as a whole.

- Mentor and raise the bar of the designers around you - through critique, pairing, and modelling what excellent design looks like.

- Drive AI thinking strategically - both in your own workflow (Claude Code, in-product changes, prototype testing) and in what we ship to users. You'll have a strong view on what makes a good AI feature in this domain vs a gimmicky one.

Why you should (and shouldn't) apply 

You should apply if: 

- You've operated at senior IC level in a modern product org and you want broader scope to influence what gets built.

- You're commercially fluent. You've made design trade-offs informed by how the product makes money, not just by user preference. You can name those trade-offs and defend them either way.

- You define what success looks like before you ship, and you read the result against it after. Metrics, support data, customer feedback - you go and look.

- You have strong, well-formed views on AI in product design and have put them into practice. You can articulate when AI is the right design solution and when it isn't.

- You move at pace on strategic work, not just on features.

You probably shouldn't apply if: 

- You're looking for the next pay band up from Senior with broadly similar expectations. This is not a "Senior+" role. Lead expects materially more scope, autonomy, judgment, and ownership of outcomes.

- You've never shipped design work where you defined a success measure upfront and checked the result afterwards. We need someone who already operates that way.

- You've never had to make a commercial trade-off - design that's user-optimal but expensive to build, or design that doesn't move retention.

- You'd struggle to explain how AI is changing what you ship, not just how you work. AI fluency is non-negotiable at this level.

- You expect to be handed a brief. At L6 you identify what's worth doing and bring the case for it.

A bit about you 

- Experience: Roughly 8+ years of Product/UX Design experience, with a track record at senior IC level. SaaS or complex product experience is strongly preferred.

- Outcomes, not artefacts: You can point to design work you've shipped where you wrote the success measure upfront and read the result after release. You know what worked, what didn't, and what you'd do differently.

- Commercial fluency: You understand how the products you've worked on make money and you've made trade-offs informed by that.

- AI: Comfortable using AI across your workflow and equally comfortable thinking strategically about AI in the products you design - what makes a good AI feature, what the failure modes are, what to build now vs later.

- Craft: Your work is exemplary and you can articulate it clearly enough to teach. You have views on interaction quality, hierarchy, motion, microcopy - and you can defend them.

- Cross-functional: Comfortable as a peer at the table with product and engineering counterparts in your domain. Drive direction; don't wait for it.

- Open to flex: This is predominantly an IC role, but we're not rigid about it. If you've line-managed before, or want to take on one or two direct reports alongside the IC work, we're open to that conversation.

Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application. 

Why join Street Group? 

🏠 Hybrid-working - you can work from home up to 4 days per week

🏖️ Guilt-Free R&R - £1000 towards a holiday after your first year with the team (we'll even cover the tax!)

💪 Joining a culture that supports your development and encourages growth

📚 £500 yearly L&D budget for your career development

🎂 Your birthday on us - we pay, you stay away

🙋 'Give something back' - 2 paid days volunteering on us

👶 Enhanced maternity, paternity & adoption pay

🧠 Mental health & well-being support via Health Assured

🧘 Regular well-being initiatives

🕒 Flexible working hours

🚂 Public transport season ticket loans

🌷 Paid menopause leave

🌞 Holiday buying scheme

🚀 Joining a new team in an exciting business with huge ambition

👥 Be a part of something bigger - everyone in our team is passionate about improving the entire property industry! It's a huge goal, but it motivates us to do better every single day

Fastned France est en pleine expansion, et en tant qu'Expansion Manager, tu seras un.e acteur.rice clé de cette croissance. 

Tes futures missions : 

- Identifier de nouveaux terrains pour y implanter nos stations de recharge rapide. 

- Analyser les nouveaux sites et monter les dossiers, d’un point de vue économique et juridique. 

- Nouer des relations commerciales avec divers types de propriétaires fonciers. 

- Négocier et conclure des contrats de bail. 

- Suivre et coordonner le développement des projets, de la signature des accords jusqu'à l’ouverture des stations. 

- Coordonner avec les services internes le bon déroulement des projets. 

- Cultiver et développer ton réseau, représenter Fastned lors d’évènements extérieurs.

Grâce à ton réseau dans l'immobilier, tu renforceras notre maillage territorial en créant de nouvelles opportunités avec des propriétaires fonciers, des promoteurs et développeurs immobiliers. La mobilité électrique est un domaine nouveau pour toi ? 

Pas de problème ! Dans le cadre de ton intégration, tu participeras à une série d’onboardings passionnants où tu apprendras tout ce qu’il faut savoir sur le monde de l’e-mobilité et de la recharge.
