Tu aimes prendre des initiatives, tu n’as pas peur de faire des erreurs et tu as soif d’apprendre ? Si tu coches également les cases suivantes, alors postule ! 

- Tu vis dans la région parisienne et tu y as déjà un réseau conséquent; 

- Tu as +3 ans d’expérience en développement immobilier ou d’enseignes ; 

- Tu es intéressé.e/animé.e par la transition énergétique ; 

- Tu as le contact facile, capable de nouer des relations durables ; 

- Tu as l’habitude de prendre la voiture pour visiter un site en pleine campagne et le train pour venir au bureau à Paris régulièrement ; 

- Tu as de solides compétences en matière de négociation et de communication ; 

- Tu comprends et sais t’exprimer en anglais ; 

- Tu as un permis de conduire valide afin de monter à bord de ta voiture de fonction électrique et voir nos beaux projets se concrétiser partout en France ! 

Nos avantages 

Chez Fastned, on travaille avec ambition pour avoir un impact réel, et on prend le temps de reconnaître et célébrer nos réussites, qu’elles soient grandes ou petites. On valorise l’équilibre vie pro / vie perso, on t’offre une vraie flexibilité de travail et nous mettons en place des initiatives family-friendly. 

Nos avantages : 

- Un budget formation et développement de 3 000€ brut par an par collaborateur, car le développement et la formation sont importants pour nous et notre secteur offre des opportunités infinies. 

- Voiture de fonction électrique avec frais de recharge couverts. 

- Carte Ticket Restaurant, 12,20€ par jour. 

- 25 jours de congés + RTT + 2 jours de Mission Days que tu peux utiliser pour contribuer aux missions de Fastned et soutenir une cause associative qui te tient à cœur. 

- Fastned prend en charge 60 % de ta mutuelle Alan et 100 % de ton salaire pendant les 30 premiers jours d’absence pour maladie/incapacité de travail. 

- Un abonnement Gymlib avec accès à un large réseau de salles de sport et studios. 

- Plan de stock options -> nous croyons à la création de valeur partagée. 

- Bien-être mental avec nilo health : accès à une plateforme de santé mentale confidentielle offrant des séances de coaching individuel avec des psychologues, des sessions de groupe et une variété d’outils. 

- Des événements festifs: Ski trip, Fastned Days, team buildings - des temps forts pour se retrouver, échanger et célébrer nos réussites. 

Envie d'en savoir plus ? 

On serait ravis d'avoir une conversation avec toi ! Envoie-nous ton CV et dis-nous en plus, pourquoi Fastned, et pourquoi toi. 

Le processus de recrutement se déroule en 4 étapes : 

- Entretien vidéo avec notre recruteuse ; 

- Entretien vidéo avec la Lead Expansion France et un Expansion Manager 

- Case study vidéo avec la Lead Expansion France, et deux membres de l’équipe ; 

- Team coffee chats dans nos locaux parisiens pour rencontrer les collègues de l’équipe France.

Process de recrutement : 

Nous nous engageons à rendre ce process aussi rapide et efficace que possible, et à maintenir une communication ouverte et transparente tout au long du process.

title: Technical Recruiter, Manufacturing
description:
Swarm Aero is redefining air power, building the largest swarming UAV and the most versatile swarming aircraft network in the world. The company is moving quickly to launch the first aircraft designed specifically for swarming, as well as the Command & Control software to mobilize swarms of thousands of heterogeneous autonomous assets and empower human operators to achieve superhuman results.

The team has created and exited multiple startups, negotiated defense deals worth billions of dollars, and designed and built 30+ novel aircraft, with aerospace experience from Scaled Composites, Airbus, Archer Aviation, Blue Origin, and Boom Supersonic.

The Role

Right now our factories are floor plans, early equipment, and a handful of people who've done this before. In a few years they need to produce aircraft at rate. You'll help find everyone in between.

You'll be a core part of our manufacturing hiring across two sites: our Oxnard HQ and a new facility in Northwest Arkansas. Early on, that means landing the few people who set the foundation. Later, it means scaling fast without lowering the bar. When manufacturing hiring is lighter, you'll flex to support other teams across the company, so you'll never be short on work or on range.

The Work

- Own full-cycle hiring across manufacturing, industrial, quality, tooling, and production roles at both sites, from technicians on the floor to the leaders running them

- Learn manufacturing well enough to follow a layout review. Composites, tooling, process development, and factory ramp: you should know what good looks like

- Recruit from where the talent actually is. Automotive, EV, consumer hardware, and high-rate industrial manufacturing are often better sources for us than legacy aerospace

- Build our Northwest Arkansas talent pipeline from zero: schools, trade programs, local manufacturers, veteran networks, and community partners

- Hire ahead of the scale-up. Build relationships today with people we may not hire for two years

- Flex to support aircraft, supply chain, operations, and other teams when manufacturing volume allows. Manufacturing always comes first

You

- Have [4+] years of full-cycle recruiting experience, with meaningful time recruiting for manufacturing, production, or hardware teams

- Know the difference between a manufacturing engineer and an industrial engineer without looking it up

- Have hired through a factory launch, production ramp, or high-growth hardware environment and liked the pace

- Can run hiring in two very different markets without either one feeling like the afterthought

- Would rather source a composites tech out of a boat builder than wait for an applicant

Bonus Points

- Recruiting experience at an EV, automotive, aerospace, or hardware company during a plant launch or ramp

- Experience hiring hourly and skilled trades at volume alongside engineering roles

- Familiarity with the Northwest Arkansas or Midwest manufacturing talent market

- Supply chain or operations recruiting experience

Why This Seat

You get to build the hiring engine for a factory before it exists, at a company where manufacturing is the whole ballgame.

How We Recruit

We're a small recruiting team building a defense company that has to win. Here's how we operate, and we hire recruiters who already work this way.

The Standard. We know the work deeply. We are not generalists hiding behind job descriptions; we study the engineering, the domain, and the landscape until we can hold a real conversation with a practitioner. Every candidate who talks to us should call it the best recruiting experience of their career, and we each bring our own personality to get there. High touch, never scripted.

How We Think. One foot old school, one foot forward: we're obsessive about the fundamentals of recruiting and restless about finding better ways to do it. We play the long game and hire for what someone will do in two and five years, not just next quarter. And we'd rather define the industry standard than follow it.

How We Operate. Mission first, always. Speed is a competitive weapon, and we use it. Quality over comfort: we'll have the harder conversation with a hiring manager before we'll make the easy hire.

title: Senior data collection operator (FR)
description:
About Genesis 

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco, London and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We're building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

The role 

General-purpose robots learn from real, dexterous human work, the kind of data that does not exist on the internet. We capture it with our own collection hardware: a person wears it, does the work, and the robot learns to do it too.

You will be a senior member of the team scaling our data collection operation in Paris, working closely with our Paris research and engineering teams and with the operation in the Bay Area.

You will help lead the day-to-day execution and quality bar on the Paris floor while remaining deeply hands-on with data collection, teleoperation, task setup, and real-robot testing. You will wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and take ownership of complex collection requests from setup through execution and quality review.

You will work shoulder to shoulder with our model engineering and research teams, turning their requests into physical demonstrations and feeding what you learn on the floor back to them. You will be expected to operate autonomously, help guide and train other operators and contribute to how the Paris operation evolves as the team grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not just run existing tasks: you will help shape how they are executed, how quality is measured, and how other operators are trained to deliver consistently.

What you will do 

- Help lead the Paris data collection floor. Set the execution and quality bar for day-to-day collection work and help the team scale effectively.

- Own complex collection setups. Take a loosely defined request and turn it into a working, repeatable collection task, including the setup, fixtures, props, environment, and procedure, with minimal support from engineering.

- Create high-quality training data. Wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and produce precise demonstrations that can be used to train our models.

- Own the full collection workflow. Go beyond collecting the data itself: review and quality-check your work, identify unusable episodes, support annotation, and help ensure that what reaches research is trainable data.

- Build repeatable tasks. Turn new collection requests into clear, repeatable processes that can be executed consistently by other operators.

- Partner with research and model engineering. Translate their requests into physical collection tasks, share observations from the floor, and iterate with them on setups and collection strategy.

- Improve the operation. Identify when a fixture, station layout, procedure, or collection method can be improved and proactively help implement those improvements.

- Write and improve the playbook. Own SOPs, quality checks, and training materials that allow the Paris operation to scale while maintaining a consistent quality bar.

- Guide other operators. Help onboard, train, and mentor operators and reinforce consistent execution across the team.

- Run real-robot testing. Partner with reliability and engineering teams to test robots on the floor, document what you observe, and help surface issues.

- Own quality. Review your own work and the team's, take direct feedback, and keep raising the bar.

What we are looking for 

- You have done precise, repetitive physical work to a high quality bar and can explain what made your work good and how you measured it. This could include data collection, teleoperation, motion capture, robotics lab work, assembly, fine craft, or another hands-on technical environment.

- Hands-on robot or glove-based data collection experience is a strong plus, but not a requirement. This kind of data collection is new, and we will teach you our specific tools and approach.

- You build, not just run. Give you a vague request and a scrappy setup, and you can turn it into a clean, repeatable task with the right fixtures, environment, process, and written procedure.

- You can operate autonomously. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex collection tasks with limited day-to-day support from engineering.

- You understand quality beyond collection. You can review your work, recognize when collected data is unusable or below the quality bar, and understand why.

- You are ready to lead. You have trained, mentored, or led others doing hands-on work and want to help establish the execution and quality standard for a growing team.

- You work well with research and engineering teams. You can translate their requests into physical collection tasks and turn what you observe during collection into useful feedback.

- You have exceptional attention to detail. You notice the moment something about the setup, hardware, environment, procedure, or collected data is off.

- You are technically handy. You are comfortable with Linux, some Python scripting to automate repetitive work, and hardware assembly and troubleshooting.

- You are comfortable in a fast-moving environment. Hardware, processes, and collection methods will evolve quickly, and you are comfortable adapting while helping improve how the team works.

- You communicate well in English. You will work daily with teams in Paris and the Bay Area across time zones. French is a plus.

- Bonus: reliability testing. You have partnered with a reliability or test team on real-robot testing.

Working conditions and role constraints 

- Work takes place in production environments and technical laboratories.

- Prolonged standing and repetitive hand and arm movements while wearing collection equipment, including gloves, head-mounted cameras, and headsets, for extended periods.

Le Responsable Métrologie garantit la conformité métrologique des équipements utilisés pour le transport des échantillons biologiques. PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITES 

Métrologie et maîtrise de la température 

• Définir et mettre en œuvre la politique métrologique de l'entreprise.

• Garantir le respect des exigences réglementaires relatives au transport des échantillons biologiques.

• Organiser les opérations de vérification, d'étalonnage et de qualification des équipements.

• Analyser les dérives et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives.

• Assurer la maîtrise et le suivi quotidien des plateformes de télésurveillance métrologique : deux solutions sont actuellement utilisées, l'une auprès d'un fournisseur couvrant la majorité du parc, l'autre auprès d'un second fournisseur actuellement en phase de test.

• Superviser l'outil interne propriétaire de l'entreprise, connecté aux équipements et générant des alertes en temps réel en cas de dérive de température.

Coordination avec le parc automobile et l'exploitation

• Coordonner avec l'Exploitation afin de limiter l'impact des interventions sur l'activité.

• Veiller à la disponibilité opérationnelle des véhicules conformes aux exigences de température.

Gestion des fournisseurs

• Suivre les contrats de maintenance et les performances des prestataires.

• Assurer une veille technologique sur les équipements de transport sous température dirigée.

Qualité et amélioration continue 

• Participer aux audits internes et externes.

• Élaborer les procédures et instructions de travail.

• Assurer le suivi des indicateurs de performance.

• Conduire les analyses de causes en cas de non-conformité.

• Proposer des actions d'amélioration continue.

• Représenter la métrologie lors des audits qualité menés directement par les clients laboratoires et préparer les éléments de preuve associés (certificats d'étalonnage, historiques de température).

ACTIVITES DECISIONNELLES 

Le Responsable Métrologie est amené à :

• valider les choix techniques des installations ;

• décider des actions à engager en cas de dérive de température ou de non-conformité ;

RELATIONS FONCTIONNELLES

En externe

PROFIL RECHERCHE 

Formation

Expérience

Compétences techniques

140 / COFRAC).

• Force de proposition.

• Capacité à coordonner plusieurs interlocuteurs.

• Réactivité face aux situations d'urgence.

Objectifs du poste 

• Garantir le maintien permanent de la chaîne de température des échantillons biologiques.

• Assurer la conformité réglementaire des équipements et des véhicules.

• Optimiser les investissements en matériels de métrologie et de transport frigorifique.

- Direction . The roadmap for FV consulting. Which capabilities, markets and problem domains we pursue, and what we decline.
- Customers. You are the face of LUBIS EDA to our key accounts and at executive level. You open the doors your managers cannot, and you carry the conversations that decide a long-term relationship.
- Organisation . Structure, standards, playbooks, talent pipelines, and the career framework in practice. You keep improving how we work, and you decide when a new technology — AI among them — changes the way we deliver.

Our formal sign-off business is growing. Our customers are getting bigger. So are our ambitions. title: Lead Product Manager - RPG
description:
Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love. We partner with studios and internally develop games, having launched over 80 titles, reached over 2 billion downloads, and seen our game All in Hole break into the global top-50 grossing charts. These are milestones, not the finish line. 

With deep expertise in product and technology, we built Homa Lab, our proprietary platform that gives developers the market intelligence, data tools, and game tech, with AI built-in, to find product–market fit fast and scale mass-market games into lasting experiences players enjoy for years.

This is our flywheel: Homa Lab helps studios spot the right ideas early, turn them into games quickly, and reach millions of players. Every launch brings back data and insights that fuel the next hit, making each turn of the loop faster, smarter, and more likely to win. AI supercharges this process, running through everything we do, from everyday tasks to our guiding principles.

What powers the loop is talent density. 220+ people from 30+ nationalities, bringing expertise from the world’s best studios and companies. We uphold ambition, curiosity, humility, and focus, and deliver with speed, excellence, and candor. Since the start, we’ve raised $165M from Headline, Northzone, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, and the founders of King, Sorare, and Spotify, people who’ve built and backed the games and platforms we admire, now supporting our drive to create the next ones.

At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment.

Mission 

As a Lead Product Manager on our RPG games, you'll play a key role in defining and owning the product roadmap for our live RPG games portfolio end-to-end, starting by turning one of our current strongest live titles into a franchise players stay with for years. You'll start with one game, and as our RPG portfolio expands, so does your scope, more titles, and a real hand in the product strategy behind them. You're shaping how Homa runs RPG as a whole.

Your main responsibilities will include:

- Define the product roadmap across one or more live RPG titles: core loop, progression pacing, monetization, and meta systems such as gacha, PvP, seasons, and guild or pass structures, with the health of the in-game economy.
- Own LiveOps end-to-end. You'll define the calendar, the events, and the loop that brings players back by a real understanding of what the team can design, produce, and sustain sprint over sprint: ambitious, but grounded.
- Lead your team. You'll have a talented but small team of product, design, and economy experts to lead towards the same goal. Your job is to give them a clear plan, raise their level, and get the best out of them.
- Oversee the monetization model. Working closely with economy, you're accountable for leading how the game balances the IAP and ad revenue growth together rather than at each other's expense.
- Drive growth, in partnership with UA. You're responsible for how the game scales on the acquisition side: working hand-in-hand with the UA team so that the player data, creative learnings, and campaign performance shapes the product roadmap.
- Cross-functional excellence. You'll work hand-in-hand with Publishing and the studios, through logic and shared KPIs, which means understanding how a game gets built and shipped end-to-end, from concept to launch.
- Set the bar. Bring genre benchmarks and proven best practices into every major call, so the team always has a clear, shared sense of what great looks like in this genre.
- Stay hands-on when it counts. This is a leadership role, but you'll stay close enough to the data and the systems to go deep personally on whatever matters most that month, rather than directing only from a distance.

This is a great opportunity to take a genuinely exceptional game and decide what it becomes: full ownership of the product, the economy, and the LiveOps of a title Homa is betting on, real autonomy over how you get there, and a clear path to leading product across our whole RPG portfolio as it grows.

Requirements 

We are looking for someone with several years of product experience on live mobile games, especially RPG, with genuine end-to-end ownership of an economy, progression system or monetization roadmap, and the humility, curiosity, ambition, and drive to make an impact fast. You're a great fit if you have:

Product & RPG expertise 

- P roduct experience on live F2P mobile games , ideally RPG/midcore, with end-to-end ownership of major features, progression, monetization or product roadmaps.
- Strong fluency in RPG mechanics and meta systems: progression, power curves, collection, PvP/social, seasons and passes, and strong mobile marketability instincts.
- Ideally, you’ve taken a title from concept/pre-launch through launch and LiveOps , or shaped product direction across multiple titles.
LiveOps & Execution 

- Deep LiveOps experience , understanding how events, content, progression and monetization work together to drive engagement and repeat spend.
- Strong track record owning features end-to-end : identify, build, ship, measure and iterate, with a practical understanding of what a live team can realistically ship and maintain , balancing ambition with feasibility.
Leadership & Ways of working 

- Strong cross-functional leadership , able to align Design, Publishing, Data, Economy, UA, Growth and external studios around the product direction.
- A strategist and builder : able to set direction and lead others, while remaining highly hands-on with the game, systems and data.
- Thrives in lean, fast-moving, high-autonomy teams with quick tests, short feedback loops and high ownership

Our Culture 

At Homa, we prioritize talent, energy, and determination over traditional credentials. We’re building a global community of brilliant, driven people who think boldly, move fast, and push boundaries. We believe true innovation comes from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and curiosity without limits. Our culture is grounded in four core values:

- Ambition : We strive for the best - we don’t settle for “good enough.”
- Humility : We recognize that we are always learning, we can always improve and grow.
- Curiosity : We continuously seek the “why” behind the “what”.
- Focus : Our curiosity takes us deeper, not wider - we dive deep into the details.
Benefits 

Building great games starts with building a great place to work. Here’s what you can expect:

- 🏥 Comprehensive Benefits: Depending on your location, you’ll enjoy a range of perks such as insurance, meal vouchers, public transport, gym memberships, and more.
- 🏢 Paris HQ Access: Enjoy a desk at our private office in a well-located WeWork building that will give you access to WeWork perks like rooftop view and designed coworking spaces.
- 🌍 Coworking Access: You will have access to WeWork spaces throughout Europe, along with all their perks and professional office environments.
- 🌐 Global Team: Collaborate in English with top-tier talent from 35+ countries, spanning Europe, the UK, the US, and more. Diversity fuels our creativity and innovation.
- ✈️ Team Gatherings: We value time together beyond the screen. Join us for occasional team gatherings, off-site retreats (Workations as we name them) to connect, recharge, and celebrate.
- 📈 Performance Reviews: We’re committed to your growth. Every six months, we reflect on your progress, recognize your achievements, and align on clear development goals.
- 💻 Equipment Support: From day one, we’ll provide everything you need to do your best work, including a home office setup allowance if you're working remotely.
Where We Hire

Our HQ in Paris is a vibrant hub of creativity, collaboration, and connection. From rooftop lunches and coffee chats to after-work apéros and community events, we’ve designed a space people genuinely enjoy - all within a cozy WeWork filled with good energy (and snacks).

We also have incredible team members across Europe - from Spain and Turkey to Germany, North Macedonia, Poland, the UK, and more. Whether you’re working from a sunny WeWork in Barcelona or your home setup in Warsaw, you’re fully part of our culture. To keep collaboration smooth, we primarily hire within European time zones (UTC to UTC+3). If you're based there - or planning to be - we’d love to hear from you!

Please note: this is one remote position open to multiple countries, not multiple openings.

- Single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomic data analysis.

- Clinical and biomedical imaging data.

- History of publications or contributions to top-tier academic journals or conferences.

- Have previously worked in a biotech / pharma / life science company.

#LI-HB1

title: Applied AI Engineer, Startups (Codex)
description:
About the team 

The Applied AI Engineering team works closely with frontier startups. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior.

This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems.

About the Role 

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex for startups, you will help developers and founders transform how they build and ship software. You’ll combine hands-on engineering, startup experience, and compelling technical communication to help teams turn the potential of AI coding tools into practical, effective workflows.

Presentations and community engagement are central to this role. You will engage developers and founders through technical talks, live demos, workshops, and programmes across the startup ecosystem, alongside targeted work with individual customers. You’ll build reusable tools and resources that extend your impact, and bring insights from developers back to OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams.

This role is well suited to someone who enjoys both hands-on building and sharing what they learn with others. You should be as excited to lead a room of developers, deliver an engaging presentation, and build relationships across the startup community as you are to explore a technical problem in code—with a focus on sustained adoption and meaningful improvements in how startups work.

In this role, you will: 

- Partner with top startups to identify where Codex can have the greatest impact on how their teams build and ship software.

- Design and lead technical talks, live demos, workshops, hackathons, and repeatable hands-on programmes that turn initial interest into sustained adoption.

- Work directly with selected customers to build Codex workflows, integrations, and automations, resolve technical blockers, and evaluate effectiveness and reliability.

- Turn successful approaches into reusable code examples, guides, and tools that help more startups succeed with Codex and OpenAI’s broader platform.

- Collaborate with account teams, developer experience, and ecosystem partners to reach developers and founders, prioritise opportunities, and drive measurable customer value.

- Translate customer experiences and developer feedback into actionable insights for OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams.

You’ll thrive in this role if you: 

- Have experience building at, founding, or working closely with early-stage startups, and understand the pace, ambiguity, and practical trade-offs involved.

- Bring strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy building practical AI applications, integrations, and developer tools.

- Are an active user of Codex or other AI coding tools, with a thoughtful perspective on how they can improve software development.

- Are a compelling communicator who enjoys presenting, delivering live demos, and leading hands-on workshops for developers and founders.

title: Senior Engineering Manager (Hands-on) - Offer
description:
Health can’t wait . 

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

🤖 The Offer Area

We’re the engine that decides what Alan sells, at what price, and on what terms. 

Every Alan member, from a 3-person startup to a public administration body with 200K+ collaborators is covered by an offer that our area designed, priced, contracted and renews every year.

We own the whole offer lifecycle for several kind of services (health insurance, life & disability insurance, employee benefits) across 4 countries. We manage an incredible business complexity and diversity in a scalable way, and most importantly, we empower others to act autonomously on it:

- Offer creation: Enabling Sales to build compliant and relevant offers themselves in minutes, with a real-time pricer and AI assistance, without waiting days for an actuary.

- Contract Lifecycle: Not only signing a contract in one go and writing the settings that become the source of truth for the rest of Alan, but also providing Business Ops with the tools they need to pilot over the years a portfolio of 100K+ contracts

- Enabling growth: We’re at the root of Alan’s Insurance stack. Our technical decisions have a long reach: Claims, Billing and many other teams depends on us. We are key to lift blockers and enable the opening of new segments or markets.

🚀 What you'll build and who you'll work with

- 🌍 One insurance stack for every country. We're replacing country-by-country code with a shared "Core Stack": one set of shared rules, with room for local differences. Spain already runs on it, and we’re now tackling France. The architecture decisions you make will shape how Alan sells insurance for the next 10 years. ( How we made our offer builder global )

- 🤖 AI-native underwriting. Insurance is complex, and most insurers need actuaries on every quote. We empower our Sales to build compliant and relevant offers themselves in minutes. AI-assisted smart alternatives, price explanations, pitching and more are already in the Sales hands, and there’s much more to build.

- 🛡️ Life & Disability as a first-class product : We’re bringing this historically smaller product at Alan to the same level of maturity as Health, with first class member XP, Ops and enabling access to a much wider population.

- 🧑‍🚀 A growing team. You'll hire it, shape it, and decide what it works on. Talent density, onboarding, feedback, and the mix of skills the area needs are yours to own.

- 🛡️ Technical direction and operational excellence. Architecture calls, quality standards and shaping the organization and incident response as we scale to more countries. And you stay hands-on: at Alan, engineering leaders are expected to build.

⚡ Why this role is special

- Dual impact : Shape both technical excellence and team growth, engineers become better while building better products

- Leadership growth : Influence engineering culture, mentor future leaders, and drive technical strategy that shapes the future of healthcare delivery

- Your users sit next to you : Hundred of Alaners use what your team ships every day. The feedback loop between building and impact is very short, which allows you to iterate and move quickly.

- Complex domain, simple software: Regulated domain, many countries, many segments… The job is to model a messy real world into a stack that stays simple and easy to extend.

- Direct business impact. We own pricing, contract lifecycle and Sales tooling. We have a direct impact on Alan’s margin and growth.

🔍 What we're looking for

We're looking for an engineering leader who gets excited about building state-of-the-art AI systems and applying them to real-world, high-stakes problems in healthcare.

Leadership experience

- 3+ years leading engineering teams, with a track record of building high performers.

- You partner with other product functions as a true equal: you shape the roadmap, name trade-offs honestly, and help the team commit to what it can actually deliver.

Technical foundations

- Experience establishing engineering excellence standards, with the ability to guide architectural decisions.

- First-hand experience shipping AI or LLM products to production is a big plus.

- You're excited and eager to keep writing code. You still review it, and you still ship some yourself.

- Comfortable with modern development practices and AI-assisted development tools.

What we value

- Curious, self-starting, humble, collaborative, and eager to grow.

- You develop people as much as you develop products.

- Ex-founders are typically a great fit in our team.

Mission alignment

- Healthcare technology and innovation excite you

- You understand that great engineering teams are built on psychological safety and continuous learning

But above all, we are looking for high potential and curiosity: make sure to show us this when you apply!

🎯 Important note: we hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you . Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply, as it can only bring learnings or success.

If you identify yourself as a woman : Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

Remember, this is just a guide, not a checklist. We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

title: Senior GL Accountant
description:
Contentsquare is the all-in-one experience intelligence platform designed to be easily used by anyone who cares about digital journeys. With our flexible and scalable platform, organizations quickly get a deep understanding of their customers’ whole online journey. 

We are a global leader in the experience analytics space, with a growing presence across 15 offices worldwide. We’re here to stay—and we’re looking for team members who are excited to drive impact and help us scale even further. 

Our aim is to create an inclusive workplace where everyone learns and succeeds. Contentsquare has built a community of individuals who are daring, understanding, and deliberate. We invite you to join us in making the complex simpler—for our customers, their customers, and each other. 

Important note: Be careful of scammers pretending to be from Contentsquare. We will never ask for money or contact you through random texts. Any communication from our in house Talent Acquisition team will only ever come from our contentsquare.com or ----- domain. For more information, visit our careers blog. 

About the job 

Reporting to the RTR Director based in Paris, you will be responsible for a range of General Accounting activities for Contentsquare SAS, the Group's largest entity and headquarters, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and completeness of the financial statements in accordance with IFRS and French GAAP.

This is a fixed-term contract starting in mid-January 2027 , to cover a parental leave.

What you’ll do 

- Support day-to-day General Ledger operations, including journal entries, account reconciliations, and accounting adjustments.

- Contribute to monthly, quarterly, and year-end closing activities in accordance with IFRS and French GAAP.

- Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual tax declarations and support statutory audits.

- Maintain accurate records of prepaid expenses, accruals, provisions, and fixed assets.

- Contribute to the preparation of internal and external financial reporting.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with teams including FP&A, Legal, HR, Procurement, and other business stakeholders.

- Contribute to process improvement initiatives and ERP system enhancements.

- Support the implementation, maintenance, and documentation of accounting policies and internal controls.

- Ensure compliance with internal accounting procedures and relevant local and international accounting standards.

What you’ll need to succeed 

- Advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

- 7+ years of experience in General Accounting , ideally gained across both an accounting firm and an in-house/corporate environment.

- Strong knowledge of IFRS is required ; knowledge of US GAAP is a plus.

- Fluency in French and English , as you will work in a truly international environment.

- Strong analytical and technical accounting skills, with excellent attention to detail.

- Ability to work autonomously, prioritize effectively, and take ownership of responsibilities.

- Highly organized, proactive, and reliable, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders.

- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, work under pressure, and meet strict reporting deadlines.

- Comfortable joining a team for a fixed-term assignment and quickly becoming operational.

Nice to have 

- Previous experience in the Tech / SaaS sector .

- Experience with Microsoft Excel , including VBA.

- Experience working with Workday Financials .

- Previous experience in an international or multi-entity organization.

Why you should join Contentsquare 

We invest in our people through career development, mentorship, social events, philanthropic activities, and competitive benefits. We are always assessing the perks we offer to ensure we’re aligned with the employees' needs. 

Here are a few we want to highlight: 

- Virtual onboarding, Hackathon, and various opportunities to interact with your team and global colleagues both on and offsite each year 

- Work flexibility: hybrid and remote work policies 

- Generous paid time-off policy (every location is different) 

- Lifestyle allowance 

- A Culture Crew in every country we’re based in to coordinate regular activities for employees to get to know each other and bond outside of work 

- Every full-time employee receives stock options, allowing them to share in the company’s success 

- We have multiple Employee Resource Groups, that offer a safe space for individuals who share common identities, life experiences, or allyship to connect, support one another, and passionately advocate for the issues close to their hearts 

- And more benefits tailored to each country

title: Senior Data Steward
description:
Offre d'Emploi : Senior Data Steward (Center of Expertise Data & AI Governance - Central) 

Notre équipe Data & AI Governance recherche un·e Senior Data Steward (f/m/d) en CDI basé·e à Lille / Paris .

Chez Decathlon, nous croyons au pouvoir du sport pour unir et inspirer. Notre mission : rendre le sport accessible au plus grand nombre, partout dans le monde. Pour y parvenir, la data est au cœur de notre stratégie, guidant chaque décision, de la conception du produit à l'expérience client. Notre défi ? La rendre gouvernée, sûre et exploitable. Tu rejoindras le Data & AI Governance Center of Expertise (CoE), une équipe dynamique de passionné·es, pour transformer notre patrimoine de données brutes en un actif certifié, auditable et actionnable, garantissant ainsi l’excellence de nos données et notre transition vers l'IA.

TA FUTURE CONTRIBUTION 

En tant que Senior Data Steward , tu seras un référent clé en Gouvernance des données pour les membres de la communauté fédérée. Tu joueras un rôle pivot dans la définition, le déploiement et l’amélioration continue des standards de gouvernance, avec un focus sur les sujets de Data Knowledge et/ou Data Quality.

Ton temps sera partagé entre :

- L'accélération de la feuille de route centrale du CoE Data Governance : définition des standards stratégiques (Data Governance by Design, référencement des exigences de qualité métier, pilotage centralisé de la qualité des données, intégration des exigences de gouvernance dans le projet Data Contract de la Data Platform, et développement du Data Knowledge / Context Layer, etc.).

- L'accompagnement d'une Digital Unit / Domaine Métier (Supply Chain, Commerce, Digital Sports ou Corporate Operations) et d'équipes Pays : piloter la pratique de Data Stewardship, accompagner la montée en maturité, co-définir et piloter la trajectoire des OKR stratégiques (ex: 95% des données critiques respectant leur seuil de qualité) et animer la communauté.

TES RESPONSABILITÉS 

Tu vas pousser l'organisation vers l'excellence dans l'exécution de la gouvernance et de la qualité des données par tous les moyens nécessaires, notamment :

- Définir et faire évoluer le cadre de Data Governance :

- Unified Trust & DQ Metrics Store : Participer à la structuration du Data Quality Metrics Store pour offrir une vision unifiée et transparente de la santé des données.

- Gouvernance & Data Contracts : Collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe Data Platform pour veiller à ce que les exigences de gouvernance, de sécurité/conformité (classification, PII) et de qualité soient nativement intégrées dans le projet Data Contract ( "Define once, apply everywhere" ).

- Data Knowledge & Context Layer : Structurer la connaissance technico-fonctionnelle dans le catalogue de données (Collibra) et promouvoir la couche de contexte ( Context Layer ) pour faciliter la découvrabilité et le lignage des données.

- Shift-Left & Remédiation : Déployer le modèle de responsabilité partagée avec les producteurs de données ( Quality by Design ) et standardiser le suivi des plans de remédiation.

- Soutenir une Digital Unit / Domaine :

- Diriger et accompagner la pratique fonctionnelle et technique du Data Stewardship au sein d'une verticale dédiée.

- Réaliser des formations techniques et méthodologiques auprès des Data Stewards, Data Owners et producteurs.

- Évaluer la maturité Data Governance du domaine et piloter les trajectoires vers la certification des actifs critiques.

- Apporter un support au quotidien et participer au recrutement des futurs coéquipiers.

- Contribuer à définir les standards d'excellence métier et évaluer le niveau d'expertise lors des recrutements de la filière Data Governance au sein des domaines.

- Animer et faire grandir la communauté des Data stewards : 

- En tant qu'expert référent, mentorer et coacher les Data Stewards moins expérimentés (Level 1 & 2) pour les faire grandir sur les pratiques de gouvernance opérationnelle. 

CE QUE TU APPORTES 

- Leadership & Influence : Tu cultives des relations solides et basées sur la confiance avec un large éventail d'interlocuteurs internes et externes, en gérant de manière experte les attentes et en favorisant l'alignement sur les objectifs stratégiques. Tu fais preuve d'une forte capacité d'influence sans autorité directe, navigues efficacement dans les dynamiques organisationnelles et géres ta hiérarchie de manière proactive. Tu escalades les enjeux critiques de façon stratégique et en garantis la résolution.

- Rigueur & Analyse : Capacité à documenter, structurer des règles et résoudre des problèmes complexes

- Expertise Métier & Gouvernance : Tu maîtrises les concepts de Data Governance, Data Quality Management, Data Lineage et Data Knowledge.

- Solide Compréhension Technique :

- Tu sais analyser, requêter et manipuler la donnée (langage SQL a minima).

- Tu comprends les grands principes d’architectures Data modernes (Data Lake, Data Products, Data Contracts,...).

- Tu as une connaissance des outils de Data Quality et de Data cataloging.

- Capacité d'articulation Tech & Business : Tu sais traduire des besoins métier complexes en exigences techniques de gouvernance et vice-versa.

STACK TECHNIQUE 

Dans ton quotidien, tu évolueras au sein d'un écosystème technologique moderne incluant :

- Gouvernance & Métadonnées : Collibra, Unity Catalog

- Data Architecture & Transformation : Databricks, DBT, Airflow, Python

QUALIFICATIONS 

- Diplôme (Licence, Master ou École d'Ingénieur) en Informatique, Data, Systèmes d'Information ou domaine connexe.

- 6-7 ans d'expérience au minimum en Data Governance, Data Stewardship, Data Quality ou gestion de programme data.

- Expérience probante dans l'animation de communautés et la conduite du changement.

- Anglais courant (niveau B2/C1 minimum) dans un environnement international.

CE QUE NOUS T’OFFRONS

The heart of a spacecraft lies in its propulsion system, and that's why we, at The Exploration Company, are dedicated to developing our own cutting-edge Propulsion Systems ensuring the highest level of efficiency and reliability in our space endeavours.

We want you as a talented CAD & Stress Analyst to help us in our mission by designing and structurally justifying the hardware that makes up our propulsion systems, with a particular focus on the Thrust Chamber Assembly(TCA). You will own parts from initial CAD layout through to final stress justification, working hand in hand with the manufacturing and test teams to bring flight hardware from concept to qualified design.

Key responsibilities

In your capacity as a CAD & Stress Analyst, you will be responsible for the on-time and on-cost design and structural justification of propulsion hardware, with the TCA as your primary scope.

Your role will be continuously evolving, but day-to-day responsibilities will include:

During the Design Phase: 

- Design the thrust chamber & injector propulsion hardware in CAD, from concept layout through to detailed design.

- Perform stress analysis (hand calculations and FEA) on designed parts to substantiate margins of safety under mechanical, thermal and pressure loads.

- Select materials and define manufacturing processes in coordination with manufacturing engineering, accounting for structural, thermal and producibility constraints.

- Work closely with propulsion, thermal and fluidic system engineers to translate functional requirements into part-level design and load cases.

- Establish and maintain interface definitions, drawings and part datasets, ensuring configuration control and traceability.

- Conduct trade studies on design options (geometry, material, manufacturing route) and justify design decisions with analysis.

- Elaborate and maintain structural analysis reports supporting design reviews and qualification.

- Support the definition of test requirements needed to validate analytical models and structural assumptions.

- Produce and maintain technical documentation of design choices and trade-offs, to a high standard, capturing analysis methods and results as to serve as reference justification for the design.

During Manufacturing, Assembly and Test Phase: 

- Support manufacturing and inspection of parts, resolving design or tolerance issues as they arise.

- Support root-cause investigations of any structural anomaly or test finding, correlating analysis with hardware behaviour.

- Update and correlate stress models and analyses based on test and inspection results.

- Support design iterations and upgrades based on test campaign outcomes.

What we would love to see from you

- A minimum of a bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical Engineering or similar degrees.

- Over 1 year of related experience in CAD design and stress analysis of mechanical or structural hardware, ideally in a propulsion, aerospace or high-reliability environment.

- Strong CAD skills, able to take a part from concept to a fully detailed, manufacturable design.

- Solid grounding in structural/stress analysis, including hand calculations and FEA (e.g. Ansys, Abaqus, or equivalent).

- Familiarity with manufacturing processes (machining, additive manufacturing, welding/brazing) and their impact on design and structural performance.

- Nice to have: CFD experience, for thermal or flow-related analysis of propulsion hardware.

- Excellent collaboration skills for working effectively across departments.

- Fluency in English.

Skills and Behaviours

- Strong oral and written communication skills.

- Strong analysis and problem-solving skills.

- Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks.

- Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done.

- Ability to communicate at all levels of the business.

- Demonstrates behaviour consistent with The Exploration Company's core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork.

- Space enthusiast, ready to change the European space industry.

Why you should join us! 

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: 

- We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

- We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them 

- We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge? 

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. 

The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable. 

All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree that any offer of employment may be conditional upon successful condition of this check. The Exploration Company partners with Zinc Work Limited located in the UK (Zinc), a third-party provider, to ensure this process as efficient and transparent as possible. 

If applicable, you will receive an email from Zinc upon acceptance of your offer with a link to a secure portal where you can provide the required information to Zinc.

title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure - Self Managed Experience (SMX)
description:
Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration , enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide , including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform . We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies , We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading. 

About the role: 

We're hiring for Self-Managed Experience (SMX) — the team responsible for making Camunda 8 deployable in a self-service way for customers who run their own infrastructure. SMX covers two areas of work: installation artifacts (Helm chart, Docker Compose, C8Run) and reference architectures & cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure).

This role sits primarily on the installation artifacts side — building, maintaining, and releasing the artifacts that ship Camunda 8 to every self-managed customer. You'll be fully embedded in that area day-to-day, but you'll work alongside the reference-architecture side of the team regularly, and SMX is actively working toward enabling every engineer to review and contribute across both stacks over time.

SMX is also shifting from a purely artifact- and ops-focused team toward one in which engineers bring customer judgment and product sense alongside technical depth. That means engaging directly with the teams closest to customers — Support, Consulting, Presales — and using that signal to help shape what we prioritize, not just executing a fully-specced ticket.

You'll find plenty of room to leave your own footprint: deployment automation, software and infrastructure testing, multi-region setups, and developer experience are all live areas of investment as the team matures from "basic install" toward full-lifecycle ownership (upgrades, backup/restore, disaster recovery).

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale 

What You’ll Be Doing: 

- Build, maintain, and release C8 distribution artifacts for self-managed customers — Helm Charts (Kubernetes), C8Run, and Docker Compose — along with their documentation.

- Improve the reliability and usability of deployment artifacts across the full customer lifecycle: installation, upgrades, and day-2 operations, not just initial deployment.

- Engage directly with internal customer-facing teams (Support, Consulting, Presales) to understand real deployment problems, and use that signal to help shape what gets prioritized — not just how it gets built. Collaborate with Development Teams, Product Management, QA, and Documentation to ship integrated, tested, and documented releases.

- Take part in the team's shared medic rotation and resolve engineering-level support cases, feeding learnings back into development.

- Contribute to the shared tooling (review, deployment, and test tooling) that SMX is building so other Camunda teams can adopt it — this is one of the team's current investment areas.

What success looks like (first ~3 months):

- Taken on your first medic rotation slot and support tickets to understand the stack, customer challenges, and deployment environments.

- Improved onboarding or documentation, turning your own ramp-up experience into concrete improvements.

- Contributed to artifact fixes, CI/CD enhancements, or test automation that strengthens release quality.

- Deliver structural improvement initiatives — a feature request, or a test/release improvement.

- Built working relationships with engineering, QA, and product peers, and started building context on the reference-architecture side of the team.

- Started forming your own view of a customer pain point from firsthand signal (support tickets, consulting feedback), not just from a ticket description.

What You Bring: 

- Ability and/or willingness to use our product, with genuine curiosity about the customer problem behind a ticket — comfortable asking "should we build this" as well as "how do we build this."

- Strong expertise in building, operating, and maintaining Helm Charts; deploying applications on Kubernetes; implementing CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions; and managing infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform).

- Ability to create clear technical documentation and communicate effectively across teams.

- A pragmatic and autonomous approach to programming and problem-solving.

- You thrive as a manager of one — you build it, you own it — and take pride in delivering maintainable, operable software.

Nice-to-haves: 

- Experience running and operating on-prem/self-hosted software on Docker.

- Familiarity with Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar observability tools.

- Working knowledge of the Go programming language.

- Exposure to cloud infrastructure/IaC (Terraform, Crossplane) — useful as SMX moves toward shared review capability across installation artifacts and reference architectures.

Must Haves: 

- 7+ years of professional experience as a software engineer , with a strong focus on backend systems and/or distributed systems.

- Proven experience leading medium‑to‑large engineering initiatives (roughly 3+ months), breaking down ambiguous problems, writing clear solution designs and project plans, coordinating with multiple teams, and driving predictable delivery.

title: Ingénieur·e en médiation scientifique et valorisation de la recherche
location: Nantes, Pays de la Loire, France
description:
1- ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE 

Grande école d’ingénieur généraliste de l’IMT-Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs de France, IMT Atlantique a pour ambition d’accompagner les transitions, de former des ingénieurs responsables et mettre l'excellence scientifique et technique au service de l'enseignement, de la recherche et de l'innovation.

Le poste est rattaché au Département interdisciplinaire en sciences sociales (DI2S) rassemblant des enseignants chercheurs et enseignantes chercheuses en sciences de gestion, sociologie, économie et droit. Sur le campus de Nantes, les recherches sont focalisées sur l’analyse des transformations des organisations et des métiers dans des systèmes sociotechniques. Trois domaines d’investigation sont privilégiés : l’industrie, la santé et l’environnement. Le ou la candidate sera affilé·e au LEMNA (Laboratoire Économie et Management Nantes Atlantique).

Plus précisément, le poste sera rattaché à la chaire RESOH [Recherche en Sécurité Organisations Hommes]. Les travaux de recherche, à l’interface de la sociologie et de la gestion, portent sur le fonctionnement des organisations à hauts risques. Partant de l’analyse du travail et des organisations de travail, il s’agit d’éclairer les dimensions socio-organisationnelles, managériales et institutionnelles contribuant à (ou empêchant) le maintien d’un niveau de fiabilité compatible avec les exigences de sécurité et de production. Les recherches de la chaire sont conduites en étroite collaboration avec des partenaires industriels et institutionnels. Elles visent à produire des connaissances scientifiques fondées sur des enquêtes de terrain, mais également à favoriser leur mise en discussion, leur appropriation et leur mobilisation par les acteurs concernés. Dans ce contexte, la chaire souhaite renforcer ses capacités de valorisation, de diffusion et d’appropriation de ses travaux, auprès de ses partenaires actuels comme, plus largement, du monde socio-économique.

2- MISSIONS 

En collaboration avec l’ensemble des enseignants-chercheurs de l’équipe (permanents et associés), les missions sont :

1- Participer à la dynamique collective de recherche au sein de la chaire 

2- Structurer et valoriser les résultats des recherches de la chaire 

3- En favoriser l’appropriation par les partenaires industriels et institutionnels de la chaire (volet interne) 

4- Contribuer au rayonnement de la chaire auprès du monde socio-économique (volet externe) 

3- ACTIVITÉS : Activité par mission 

- Participer à la dynamique collective de recherche au sein de la chaire 

· contribue activement aux réunions de coordination, espaces de discussion et séminaires de recherche (au sein de l’équipe de recherche RESOH et avec les partenaires)

2. Valoriser et diffuser les résultats des recherches de la chaire 

· cartographie les principaux travaux, résultats et productions de la chaire ;

· identifie les publics susceptibles d’être intéressés par ces résultats ;

· analyse leurs besoins et leurs attentes ;

· contribue à définir des stratégies de valorisation et de communication adaptées aux différents projets ;

· contribue à l’organisation des événements scientifiques (journée d’étude, colloque, etc.) ;

· transforme les résultats scientifiques en ressources accessibles à des publics non spécialistes, sans en perdre la rigueur, la nuance ni la portée scientifique (synthèses, notes de recherche, fiches thématiques, supports de présentation, contenus numériques ou autres formats adaptés aux publics visés).

3. Favoriser l’appropriation des travaux de recherche par les partenaires industriels et institutionnels de la chaire (volet interne)

title: Doctorant(e) - "Vers un bâtiment low-tech : caractériser et réduire les dépendances liées à la maintenance et à l'entretien du bâti face au changement climatique"
description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable . Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain .

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol. 

Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles. 

📊 Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles. 

✨ Une recherche interdisciplinaire à fort impact, où l’humain est toujours au centre. 

Cette thèse de doctorat sera rattachée au département Génie de l'Environnement pour les Organisations (GEO), membre du Laboratoire CNRS UMR 5600 Environnement Ville et Société (EVS). Pour répondre aux enjeux des transitions écologique, énergétique et industrielle, le département GEO accompagne les acteurs des territoires (acteurs publics et privés) vers une meilleure prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux et de résilience territoriale. Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables.

🏠 Contexte 

Présentation du sujet 

Le changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023).

Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes.

En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées.

Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la « lowtech » à l'interface entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales. Les compétences et l'expérience acquises trouveront une résonance particulière dans un secteur en pleine mutation, où la maîtrise des dépendances techniques, économiques et organisationnelles devient un enjeu central pour la soutenabilité des bâtiments et de leur exploitation.

Contexte scientifique 

La littérature consacrée à la low-tech s'est structurée ces dernières années autour d'une critique de la fuite en avant technologique et des dépendances qu'elle engendre (Bihouix, 2014 ; Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique.

Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants.

La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques ; replacée à l'échelle urbaine, elle révèle des réseaux d'acteurs, des filières, des compétences localement disponibles ou absentes, et des effets de dépendance mutualisés.

Contexte opérationnel 

Du côté des acteurs institutionnels et économiques, de nombreux outils accompagnent aujourd'hui la gestion technique du patrimoine bâti. Nous pouvons citer :

- les outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO) et les plateformes de gestion technique du bâtiment (GTB) ;

- les démarches de modélisation des données du bâtiment (BIM d'exploitation, jumeaux numériques) et les labels associés à la connectivité des bâtiments ;

- les contrats d'exploitation et de maintenance externalisés, et les dispositifs de garantie de performance énergétique ;

- les démarches et retours d'expérience issus de la mouvance low-tech (chantiers démonstrateurs, guides praticiens, réseaux associatifs).

Ces dispositifs partagent une orientation commune : ils visent à optimiser la conduite de la maintenance, rarement à interroger les dépendances qu'elle installe. Les démarches low-tech, à l'inverse, portent cette interrogation mais restent au stade de l'expérimentation ponctuelle, sans cadre d'évaluation partagé ni capacité de généralisation à l'échelle d'un parc ou d'un territoire.

Il en résulte, en l'état des connaissances aussi bien scientifiques qu'opérationnelles, qu'il n'existe pas de méthode permettant de rendre visibles et de qualifier les dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments, ni d'évaluer dans quelle mesure une approche low-tech permettrait de les réduire.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous 

Démarche de la thèse 

L'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments.

Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS . Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux.

Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités).

Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs.

Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées.

Verrous scientifiques : 

- Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux)

- Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponibles

- Évaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établies

- Articulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèles

Objectifs de développement durable rattachés : 

ODD 11 – Villes et communautés durables ·

ODD 12 – Consommation et production responsables

ODD 13 – Mesures relatives à la lutte contre les changements climatiques.

🔍 Ce que nous recherchons 

Formation : Bac +5 en ingénierie généraliste, sciences de l'environnement, génie civil ou énergétique du bâtiment, géographie/aménagement, ou discipline connexe. Une formation ou une sensibilité aux sciences humaines et sociales (sociologie des techniques, STS, économie de la fonctionnalité) serait un plus.

title: Senior Security Engineer, Software
description:
The Security Team of Scopely Explore (formerly known as Niantic) seeks a Senior Security Engineer to improve the security posture of our software development lifecycle, applications, and build infrastructure.

Scopely Explore, known for global hits like Pokémon GO, Monster Hunter Now, and Pikmin Bloom is now part of Scopely, home to games like Monopoly GO!, Stumble Guys, and Star Trek Fleet Command. Together, we engage billions of players worldwide, and we need your expertise to keep them safe!

Do you want to help secure one of the most widely used gaming platforms on the planet? We seek creative and dedicated engineers with excellent technical judgment, strong interpersonal skills, and an eagerness to embrace new technologies.

What You’ll Do 

- Implement and maintain agentic or AI-enabled workflows to speed-up common security tasks.

- Perform security reviews and audits of platform and application software throughout design and launch.

- Provide guidance and expertise to product and operations teams across Scopely.

- Design, build and maintain automation and tooling that amplify the Security Team’s impact and improve the developer experience.

- Drive initiatives in security architecture, application scanning, fuzzing, and other proactive defenses.

- Contribute to hardening efforts across in-house libraries, CI/CD systems, and cloud/container environments.

- Be responsible for third-party library reviews and manage vulnerability remediation.

- Educate engineers on secure coding practices and help standardize security across teams.

- Engage in red-team exercises and coordinate with internal teams and external pentesting partners.

Qualifications 

- Bachelors in Computer Science or related field

- 5+ years of experience in a global company with cloud-centric infrastructure (preferably GCP).

- You have implemented services and applications with the help of AI tools like Claude, Codex, OpenCode or Gemini and are adept in the use of these tools and adjacent technologies (RAG, MCP, etc). 

- You are capable of creating automation, agentic workflows and tooling to reliably solve problems that scale to the whole enterprise. 

- You have in-depth experience in hardening distributed web services, cloud services and platform architectures.

- You can demonstrate strong programming skills (preferably Go or Java) and a deep understanding of common vulnerability classes and exploitation patterns across modern stacks.

- Excellent communication skills and experience collaborating across distributed teams.

Bonus Points... 

- Have participated in red-team operations or managed mitigation tracking.

- Possess deep familiarity with build systems, artifact repositories, or large-scale infrastructure.

- Have delivered privacy-focused solutions for user-facing services.

- Have experience in code quality management or security champion programs.

- Have worked in a customer-centric engineering culture and value pragmatic, scalable solutions. 

- Can demonstrate hands-on experience or research in the area of AI security and safety. 

About Scopely

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit: https://www.scopely.com/ .
