title: Remote Head of UX (m/f/d)
description:
About RoomPriceGenie ✨🧞‍♂️

Founded in 2017, RoomPriceGenie is dedicated to helping hoteliers around the globe achieve optimal pricing. 🌍 We understand that many small hotels face challenges with digitalization, making their operations increasingly complex and often resulting in lost revenue. This is where we come in!

We have developed a powerful solution that enables hotels to set the right prices in just seconds. ⏱️ Our state-of-the-art algorithm analyzes both internal hotel data and market trends to recommend pricing strategies that enhance revenue and improve booking rates. 

With customers spanning the globe—from the USA and Canada to Iceland, South Africa, China, Slovenia, Italy, and the UK—RoomPriceGenie has made a meaningful impact in the hospitality industry, and our clients love the results. ❤️

Now, we are excited to expand our customer base and spread the word about how we can support hoteliers in optimizing their pricing strategies. We invite you to join us on this journey! We actively encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds to enrich our team and drive innovation. 

Your Role 

As the Head of UX at RoomPriceGenie, you'll lead our small but mighty design and research team of two product designers and one user researcher.

This isn't an IC role where you'll be pushing pixels or running sessions yourself. It's a leadership role focused on building the function, championing the team, and setting them up for success.

You'll set the strategic direction for how design and research operates, advocate for the team at leadership level, and create the conditions for your people to do their best work. You'll also play a key role in raising design and research maturity across the wider product organisation — guiding better decisions through clearer systems, guidelines, and shared insight.

Key Responsibilities 

Leadership Representation & Advocacy

- Champion design and research as a strategic partner that shapes the roadmap.

- Partner with Product Leadership to translate strategic business priorities into a clear, sequenced roadmap for Design & Research.

Strategic Direction & Vision

- Set a clear vision for the design and research function — defining what success looks like, where it's heading, and how it contributes to the company's overall strategy.

- Raise design and research maturity by providing constructive critique and quality oversight to support high-quality product outcomes.

- Create the space for the team to work on foundational initiatives that scale team impact. For example: evolving the component library into a robust design system and establishing clear design and content playbooks to drive consistency, efficiency, and quality.

AI Operations & Enablement

- Set the strategic direction for how AI fits into the design & research workflow — where it accelerates, where craft stays human, and set clear guardrails for how the wider org uses it.

- Foster a culture where the team integrates AI into product work — evolving their craft and building fluency through practice.

- Ensure designers and researchers play a key role in shaping product and AI direction, grounding decisions in user insight and design perspective.

Stakeholder Collaboration

- Advocate for Design Thinking to be embedded throughout the product life cycle, shaping ideas and guiding decisions.

- Proactively identify large, strategic UX opportunities that span across the product.

- Navigate competing priorities between leadership direction and team capacity, ensuring the team stays focused on high-impact work.

Team Development & Coaching

- Provide ongoing coaching, mentoring, and constructive feedback through regular one-to-ones — focused on the development and growth of your team.

- Build clear career frameworks and progression paths for Design and Research.

- Encourage continuous learning, adaptability, and development within the team.

Your Profile 

- A genuine understanding of both design and research disciplines, even if your background leans more toward one. You don't need to be an expert in both, but you need to value and support both equally.

- Proven experience in a senior design leadership role is required — you've owned a function, led teams of designers and researchers, and have a track record of influencing product direction at the leadership level.

- A track record of advocating for both disciplines at the leadership level and influencing product strategy, not just delivering on it.

- Experience building or maturing a design function: establishing processes, systems, playbooks, or ways of working from the ground up.

- Curiosity about AI and how it's changing the way design and research teams work — you don't need to be an expert, but you should be excited about figuring this out with the team.

Your Soft Skills 

- A compassionate, proactive leadership style that creates emotional safety for the people around you.

- Confident navigating difficult stakeholder dynamics without losing your composure or your team's trust.

- Strong communicator who can translate design value into language that resonates with leadership, product, and engineering.

- Comfortable giving and receiving direct feedback — you see it as a gift.

Nice to Have 

- Experience in or familiarity with the hotel or travel industry.

- Familiarity with building or scaling teams.

- Experience building and maintaining a design system.

- Experience working in scale-ups or startups — you're comfortable with ambiguity and thrive in environments that are still finding their shape.

What We Offer at RoomPriceGenie 💪

At RoomPriceGenie, we don’t just offer jobs; we offer an adventure! 🚀 Join us in an exciting startup atmosphere where you can grow your career while changing the world for tens of thousands of independent hoteliers. 🌍 Our global and diverse team is fueled by passion and a shared mission. We thrive in a culture that’s all about transparency, respect, and making a real impact together. 

Here’s what you can expect when you become part of our Genie family:

- Remote-First Model : Work from (almost!) anywhere. 🌍🧑‍💻 Some roles need you in a specific country or time zone — we'll always flag that in the job ad. And whenever you like, come co-work with us in Mannheim, Berlin, or Sydney. 🏢

- One Team, One Vision, One Goal: We’re in this together! 🤝 Our Genies are laser-focused on our mission, collaborating to make magic happen. ✨ It’s no wonder we score a stellar 9.3 from our team members! 🌟

- Epic Team Gatherings: Every year, we bring our global crew together 🌎 for a week of networking, brainstorming, and fun. 🎉 Plus, enjoy regular hangouts in our offices to keep the camaraderie alive.

- Growth and Development: We’re all about lifelong learning! 📚 Level up your skills with personal and professional development opportunities. You’ll even snag up to three extra days off each year to focus on your growth. 📈

- 5 Years? 5 Weeks! Stick with us, and we’ll reward your loyalty. After five years, you’ll earn an incredible five weeks of bonus vacation time 🏖️ to recharge and explore the world. 🌍

- Birthday Celebrations: It’s your day, so take it off! 🎂 Celebrate your birthday the way you want, guilt-free.

- Flexible Hours: We get it—life happens! ⏰ We offer flexible working hours to help you balance your work and personal life seamlessly.

- Wellbeing Matters: Your mental health is a top priority. 🧘 Every Genie gets access to Headspace, the leading meditation app, to help you cultivate a happier, healthier, and more zen life. 🌿

- BetterHelp Support: We also offer BetterHelp , a professional online therapy and counseling platform, giving you additional support whenever you need it. 💛🧠

title: AIT Test Engineer

Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

We are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refueled in orbit, and which carries cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.

We want you as a talented AIT Test Engineer to help us in our mission by making sure that NYX can be integrated.

You will be successful in this role if you are able to help us:

- Prepare, execute and manage the internal or external dynamic testing (vibration test, shock tests,...) of several sub-systems (electronic, fittings, weldings...) and internally developed prototypes

- Prepare, execute and manage the internal or external thermal testing (cycling, TVAC...) of several sub-systems and internally developed prototypes

- Write documentation prior and post integration and test activities

- Prepare, execute and manage other testing activities in AIT domain (e.g.: parachute, EMC, mechanisms, Structural Test Model...)

- Support mechanical integration activities needed on Nyx Capsule

Key Responsibilities

- You will manage the testing activities from definition of requirements to post-test reviews

- You will be responsible of writing, reviewing and executing procedures detailing the setups for integration and tests (in Epsilon3, ODOO, Team Center)

- You will be responsible for the execution of the tests performed in-house with internal equipment (vibration test bench, thermal vacuum chamber, shock test rig, ...)

- You will be responsible for the execution of the tests performed in external facilities

- You will be responsible of the procurement (or rental) of instrumentation and its installation on the items to test

- You will be expected to interact with other AIT engineers and technicians but also with external stakeholders

- You will be largely involved in the resolutions of anomalies happening during the integration and tests

- You will manage the reports to be done at the end of the operations/tests

- You will give your feedback and report on any blockage or problem during the testing and will work to propose improvements and fixes

- You will be asked to support the qualification plans of new processes within AIT (welding, fittings...)

- You will be supporting the Purchase of all the equipment (COTS or not) needed to run the testing activities (Tools, generic GSE)

- You will be working with AIT technicians and MGSE team to define needs of machined parts and/or tools (proposing design, follow up with MGSE team)

Additional Requirements

- Versatile, in order to support several activities depending on the workload

- Being able to manage several topics at the same time (preparation of next tests and execution in parallel)

- Proficient in following safety standards and maintaining quality control during all assembly and test operations.

Qualifications and experience

- Engineering degree (Master or PhD) in mechanical science, instrumentation/test or equivalent

title: Full Stack Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
TL;DR Join GlassDollar and help build the system some of Europe's largest companies use to find, test, and adopt startup technology.
We're looking for an engineer who wants considerably more responsibility than "implement what's in the ticket". You'll take an ambiguous problem, shape it together with product, make the important technical decisions, ship it, and stay close enough to see whether it worked.
We expect you to have opinions. We also expect you to be good enough to change them.

The problem we're solving Large organisations are remarkably good at accumulating problems. A company with 100,000 employees can have thousands of operational challenges across its business units. Somewhere outside that organisation, a startup has probably already built part of the solution. Getting those two things to meet still happens through spreadsheets, long email threads, and meetings whose primary output is another meeting.
GlassDollar OS is the operating system for venture clienting: problem → startup discovery → evaluation → PoC → adoption, in one repeatable workflow.
Our customers are some of Europe's largest organisations, so the software has to move quickly and behave like something an enterprise can depend on. That tension creates the interesting engineering problems.

What we're looking for You can take a problem further than the ticket. Work often starts with something incomplete, like "customers need a better way to manage X". You'll shape the problem with product, challenge assumptions, and decide what belongs in this iteration. Strong opinions about what we build, not only how, are expected here.

You care about product. You want to know who you're building for, why the problem matters, and what success looks like. That context should shape your technical decisions.

You have technical judgement. There is rarely one correct architecture. You know when the boring solution beats the ambitious one, when an abstraction helps and when it hides the problem, and when a small feature is about to create six months of technical debt. We expect you to reason about API boundaries, data models, permissions, performance, failure modes, testing, observability, and rollout, and to raise concerns with a clear argument attached.

You make the system better, not just the feature. You fix the spreading pattern rather than the single instance, make an API easier for the next person, and improve tests because the current setup makes everyone afraid to deploy. Your impact should show beyond the pull requests with your name on them.

You can work across the stack. A feature might run from a React interaction through GraphQL into a Node service, a schema redesign, a permissions update, and a safe migration for existing customers. Curiosity to follow the problem matters more than equal depth everywhere.

You own quality. We have QA. That's not where quality begins. What breaks if this request happens twice? What happens with old data, or when the API fails halfway through? We use Playwright and Jest alongside reviews and monitoring. The goal isn't coverage, it's confidence.

You communicate like your decisions will matter later. Six months from now, somebody should understand an important decision without digging through seventeen Slack messages and a deleted Notion comment. That means writing things down when they matter, explaining trade-offs clearly, giving useful code reviews, and surfacing risks before they become incidents.

You raise the engineering bar around you. You do not need a management title to have influence. Find the hole in an architecture, unblock someone without taking the keyboard away, disagree without turning every decision into a referendum. As you earn trust, you’ll naturally become the person people bring harder problems to.

What you'll do Over your first year: 
- Enterprise integrations: into our customers' systems, data, identity providers, and workflows. This is what turns GlassDollar from software somebody logs into, into infrastructure their organisation operates on.
- APIs and MCP: public REST APIs and MCP servers for our customers, their engineers, and increasingly their AI agents. The interesting part isn't exposing endpoints, it's designing an external platform we'll still be happy supporting years from now.
- AI inside real workflows: embeddings, vector search, and LLMs across a large database of startups and corporate innovation data. We're less interested in adding a ✨ button to everything than in finding places where AI removes real work.
- Workflow automation: triggers, notifications, and automation that replace humans moving information between systems.
- Core product engineering: React interfaces, APIs, PostgreSQL queries, permissions, migrations, performance work, and the occasional bug whose root cause makes everybody stare silently at their screen.
Our stack - Frontend: TypeScript, React, Material UI, Apollo Client, Playwright
- Backend: Node.js, GraphQL, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Jest
- Infrastructure: AWS, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Sentry
- Increasingly: LLM APIs, embeddings, vector search, MCP, AI-assisted engineering workflows
You don't need experience with every item. Reasoning about systems matters more to us than having memorised our exact stack. 

Requirements - Substantial production experience with TypeScript, React, and Node.js
- Comfortable reasoning about relational databases, not just the ORM
- Can independently take a feature from unclear starting point to production
- Can read unfamiliar code without immediately proposing a rewrite

Nice to have: 
- Experience with GraphQL, Prisma, or PostgreSQL at scale
- Exposure to LLM APIs, embeddings, or vector search
- Experience owning systems, not just features
Don't check every box? Apply anyway. We'd rather have the conversation than lose someone over a bullet point.

How we hire How we work We're a small engineering team, so there are fewer places for responsibility to disappear and no chain of five people between you and a decision. We prefer written context over meetings the calendar invented, and working software over elaborate process.
Quickly doesn't mean carelessly. Sometimes the fastest route is the simple version today, sometimes it's another day on a foundation twenty future features will sit on. Knowing which situation you're in is part of the job. Expect to ship to production very early.

How we hire No seven-stage endurance test. No algorithm trivia disconnected from the work.
- Intro. You, us, and whether this is the environment you're actually looking for.
- Technical conversation. We go deep on something difficult you've built: the decisions, the alternatives, what you'd do differently now.
- Technical assessment. Usually live coding on a realistic problem, sometimes a small proof of concept instead. We care how you think, not whether your solution matches ours.
- Offer. If there's strong mutual conviction, we move.

One last thing Job descriptions have a habit of producing candidates who optimise themselves against bullet points. Please don't. If you're reading this thinking "I can do most of this, but I haven't worked with MCP", apply.
Strong fundamentals, meaningful software shipped, and a bias toward ownership are what we're looking for. The rest is learnable.

- Run the experiment, and read it honestly. Design a testable change, get it instrumented properly, and analyse the outcome. That includes reporting the tests that did not work, and saying what you would do differently.

- Talk to neighbours. Experiments tell you what happened, not what people needed. You will spend real time with the people who use this, because you cannot A/B test your way to understanding somebody.

- Direct AI, and spend your judgment where it counts. AI produces a lot of our first-pass design. You will brief it, push back on it, and hold the quality bar, so your own hours go to the thinking a model cannot do.

title: Consultant
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

Location 

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with occasional visits to customers across the DACH region.

As team collaboration is of great importance to us, we highly encourage team members to join us in Zurich at least once a month. These visits are financially supported by BLP.

About the role 

For a process to run autonomously, four things have to line up: the technology, the process itself, the data behind it, and the people who work with it. That alignment does not happen at go-live. It happens in the months after, and that is where this role sits.

Our customers go live with a working solution. What they do not have on day one is an organisation that operates in an AI-native way. Processes were designed around people checking things. Data was maintained well enough for humans to interpret. Teams know the old workarounds better than the new system. Your job is to lead that transition, from a process that is automated in parts to a process that genuinely runs on its own.

That means working across every level of the customer's organisation. With operational teams you build understanding and find where automation is actually blocked. With department leads you challenge the process rules that make full automation impossible, and drive the decisions that change them. And you use the right lever for each blocker, because they are all different: some are a data clean-up you coordinate with the customer, some are a training and adoption gap, some need a custom agent, and some are structural and belong with our engineering teams.

You do not do this alone. You enable the customer's core team to solve their own issues, you work with our Customer Success Engineers on the technical side, and you use the Customer Success Manager to get decisions made where you need commercial weight. For our smaller customers, where there is no Customer Success Manager, you are the escalation point yourself.

You own customer health. Your sharpest measure of it is the automation rate.

What you'll do 

- Own customer health across your portfolio, measured first and foremost by automation rates.

- Lead the transition to AI-native ways of working: identify what blocks automation, and pick the right way to solve each blocker.

- Work with operational teams on enablement and adoption, so people work efficiently with blp rather than around it.

- Challenge process rules that prevent automation, and drive improvements with the department leads who can decide.

- Coordinate data clean-up with the customer where master data quality is capping what automation can reach.

- Enable the customer's core team to resolve issues themselves, and reduce what has to come to us at all.

- Identify where a custom agent solves the problem, and where the issue is structural and belongs with our engineering teams.

- Collaborate with Customer Success Engineers on technical topics, and with the Customer Success Manager to get decisions made.

- For customers without a Customer Success Manager, act as the escalation point for SLA breaches and own continuity of operations.

- Direct the AI Automation Specialists working on your accounts.

What we're really looking for 

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

- Process Excellence – You understand core business processes deeply, P2P and O2C, and you can see why a process is shaped the way it is and what it could look like instead.

- Client Hands – You bring customers with you. You are strict on the things that matter and flexible on the things that do not, you understand the context people are working in, and you have more than one way of convincing them.

- Ownership & Autonomy – You take a customer from live to high automation without being told the steps.

- Comfort in the Data – You go into the numbers yourself to find where automation is leaking.

- Problem Solving & Critical Thinking – You separate a configuration symptom from a process cause, and pick the right lever for each.

What you'll bring 

- Master's degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

- 3+ years of experience in consulting, process improvement, shared services, or ERP process ownership.

- Deep working knowledge of at least one core business process end to end, purchase-to-pay or order-to-cash. This is a prerequisite, not a nice to have.

- Demonstrable experience changing how a finance, procurement or supply chain team actually works, not only advising on it.

- Strong analytical skills. You are comfortable working with process and transaction data directly.

- Confident facilitating workshops with operational teams and presenting to their leadership.

- Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.

- Bonus points for experience with ERP systems, accounts payable or order management processes, or AI-driven SaaS.

What you'll get 

- High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.

- Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.

- Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.

- Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.

- Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.

- Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

- Technology exposure – be at the forefront of emerging technologies and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.

- Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

Location 

This is a full-time position based at our HQ in Munich or Cologne.

About the role 

You solve the hard technical problems on live systems.

Once a customer is running on blp, their processes are business critical. Invoices post or they do not. Orders flow or they sit. Our support organisation resolves most of what comes in, and a lot of it is genuinely well handled by people early in their career. What is left is yours: the cases where the cause is not obvious, where it crosses systems, data and process logic at once, where the same symptom has three possible explanations and only one of them is right.

That is the job. Not a queue, and not the easy half of one. Everything difficult that comes out of the run phase lands with you.

Two things sit alongside the case work, and they are what make this a senior job rather than a harder version of a junior one.

Stabilising accounts 
When an account's health goes bad, you go in and stabilise it. Not as a permanent assignment, but as a small, highly skilled squad that takes a customer whose numbers or whose confidence have slipped, works out what is actually wrong across the whole picture, fixes it, and hands back a customer who is running properly again. It is the most concentrated version of this work there is.

Taking effort out permanently 
Anything that keeps arriving in the queue is a signal, and the answer is usually not more people answering it. It might be better self-service for customers, a customer-facing assistant that resolves the routine questions before they reach us, better diagnostics, or a change in how something is configured at deployment so the problem never occurs. You are expected to find those, make the case, and drive them through. That is how a support organisation scales without scaling headcount one for one, and it is value the customer feels directly.

You work across the boundary between what our platform does, what the customer's ERP does, and what their data actually looks like. You are the one who can read a failing case end to end and say what really happened, and then say credibly whether the fix is configuration, data, process, or a genuine product issue. When it is a product issue, you are the counterpart to our engineering and product teams: you bring the evidence, and because you have seen the same structural problem across several customers, your case is the one that moves the roadmap.

You are also how this function gets better rather than just bigger. The diagnostic tooling, the patterns, the documentation that lets a first-year person resolve what used to take a senior one: that is yours to build. And the interns and specialists coming through the team learn this craft from you.

You do not deliver integrations and you do not run go-lives. Our integrations engineers and technical project managers own that. You own what happens once it is live and it is challenging.

What you'll do 

- Own the technically difficult cases from our live customer base, end to end, to a verified root cause.

- Diagnose across boundaries: platform behaviour, ERP behaviour, master data and process logic.

- Decide what the real fix is, and make it: configuration, data, process, or a case for engineering.

- Go into accounts with a deteriorating health score, diagnose across the whole picture, stabilise them and hand them back running properly.

- Drive strategic initiatives that permanently reduce effort and improve the customer experience, from better diagnostics to customer-facing self-service and assistants.

- Act as the counterpart to Product and Engineering, with evidence strong enough to change priorities.

- Recognise structural problems across customers and push for them to be solved once.

- Build the diagnostic tooling, patterns and documentation that raise what the rest of the team can resolve alone.

- Mentor interns and earlier-career colleagues, and raise the technical bar of the function.

- Support Consultants and Customer Success Managers on the technical substance of customer escalations.

What we're really looking for 

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

- Root Cause, Not Symptom – You are not finished when it stops happening. You are finished when you know why.

- Cross-Boundary Reasoning – You hold platform, ERP, data and process in your head at once and find where the truth is.

- Credible Both Ways – You explain the same problem to an engineer and to a CFO, and both of them believe you.

- Leverage – Your instinct is to remove the next hundred cases, not only to close this one. You would rather build the thing that makes a problem stop arriving.

- Calm Under Escalation – When a business-critical process is stopped, you get more precise rather than faster.

- Stabilizer Under Pressure : An unhappy client is not a fire to put out. It is a relationship to rebuild. You bring the temperature down, put structure back into the account, and align next steps so trust returns, not just silence

What you'll bring 

- Master's degree in a STEM field: computer science, engineering, information systems, mathematics, physics or similar. Strong candidates from a related field are welcome to make their case.

- 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: application support at depth, technical consulting, solution engineering, integration engineering or equivalent.

- Demonstrable debugging ability across systems, not only within one. APIs, data mapping, interfaces, logs.

- Comfortable with data. SQL or equivalent, and the instinct to check rather than assume.

- German and English, both fluent. This is a hard requirement. Our customers work in German every day and our internal work runs in English.

- Nice to have: ERP experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or similar, scripting in any language, or exposure to workflow automation and process mining.

What you'll get 

- The hard problems, not the queue.

- Influence on the product, with a direct line to Engineering and Product.

- Room to shape the function, since the practice is still being built.

- Real growth – the path from here leads into Consulting, technical leadership within Customer Success, or Product.

- Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.

- Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

- Visits & offsites – including collaborative team offsites.

This is a six-month internship based in Munich or Cologne. This is an in-person role. You learn this job by sitting next to people who already do it, and that does not work remotely.

About the role 

Think of this role as the modern Sherlock Holmes — new puzzles to solve and new people to work with, every single day. 
This role sits exactly at the intersection of technology and business, and that is not a figure of speech. On one side you are in the system, in the data, working out what actually happened. On the other you are on a call with a finance team explaining it and agreeing what to do. You need both, every day.

Our customers run their finance and supply chain processes on blp. When something does not behave the way they expected, a document that did not post, an exception that should have resolved itself, a number in a dashboard that looks wrong, they write to us. That is where your work starts, and it is also where you become the face of blp for that customer. What reaches them is you: your answer, your explanation, your judgement about what to do next.

You will not be reading from a script and escalating. You investigate what the system did, what the data says and what the customer's process actually requires. You have the access and the authority to change configuration when that is the answer. And when it is not, you know who to bring in and what to give them.

The role grows with you. You start on cases where the pattern is known and someone is close by. As your expertise builds you take the harder ones, and your exposure to customers grows with it: from written answers, to calls, to being in the room when a customer wants their most pressing problem solved now.

This goes well beyond tickets. We are a fast-moving organisation and a lot of what needs to exist does not exist yet. You will take on and drive initiatives that make the whole operation scale: a recurring problem that should be solved once rather than fifty times, a piece of tooling that does not exist, a way of working that has outgrown itself. Interns here have shipped things that the team still uses.

How we think about ownership 
You will be given real work with real consequences, early, because that is the only way anyone learns this job properly. The other half of that is judgement: explore and decide for yourself where you can, and pull someone in when something critical is on the line. Knowing which situation you are in is part of the skill, and nobody will hold it against you for asking. What matters is that you are the face of blp to that customer, and that you take that seriously.

Most of our customers work in German and you will be in front of them from early on. That is uncomfortable for about three weeks and then it is the best part of the job.

This is a real internship, not an observation post. You will be trusted with live customers quickly, with people close by while you learn.

What you'll do 

- Answer incoming customer requests through our support channel, and be the person they hear back from.

- Own incidents end to end: investigate, resolve, and confirm with the customer that it is actually fixed.

- Work out why a workflow, document or posting did not behave as expected.

- Adjust configuration where that is the right fix.

- Recognise when a problem is bigger than one case, and hand it on with proper evidence.

- Join customer calls to work through urgent issues directly, as your experience grows.

- Take on initiatives beyond the queue: things that should be fixed once rather than answered repeatedly.

- Document what you learn so the next person does not have to learn it twice.

What we're really looking for 

We do not expect you to know ERP systems. We expect you to be the kind of person who gets to the bottom of things.

- TSO/DSO hierarchy and the connection/integration process.

- Redispatch 3.0 regulatory framework.

- Travel: Occasional travel may be required.

- Knowledge of industrial communication protocols: IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25 (wind), OPC-UA, Modbus , or similar IEC protocols.

- Familiarity with CLI tools for configuring, diagnosing, and maintaining hardware or network connections in remote, Linux-based environments.

We're expanding fast across New York, Europe, and Brazil - and we're just getting started.

We’re still a small team, which means the people who join now will have an outsized influence on the product, the engineering culture, and the company we become.

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior or Staff Product Engineer to help build the next generation of Passionfroot.

You’ll work across the full stack on both our core platform and Zest, our AI Campaign Manager for creator marketing. That could mean designing a new workflow for managing creator campaigns, making collaboration data feel instant, or turning models, search, and product context into a reliable AI experience that customers can trust.

We don’t separate “AI engineering” from “product engineering.” AI is becoming part of how the product works, but great product fundamentals still matter: understanding the user, shaping the problem, choosing the right architecture, building a thoughtful experience, and operating it reliably in production.

You’ll work closely with the founders, design, and customers to take important problems from early exploration to shipped product.

We’re a team of six engineers, and staying small is deliberate. It means you can have an idea on Monday and have customers using it by Thursday—without layers of sprint ceremonies or alignment meetings in between. The flip side is real ownership: you need to exercise strong judgment, communicate your decisions, and think through their consequences rather than wait for someone else to catch them.

📍This role is based in our Berlin or São Paulo offices with a hybrid work model. We are also open to candidates who are willing to relocate to either area. 

What you’ll do

- Own meaningful product areas from problem definition through architecture, implementation, launch, and iteration.

- Build customer-facing features across our marketplace, campaign management, collaboration, payments, analytics, and creator workflows.

- Help make Zest an indispensable part of how modern companies run creator-led growth.

- Turn foundation models into structured, reliable product experiences—not just impressive prototypes.

- Work on intelligent workflows involving agents, tools, retrieval, search, recommendations, and generated interfaces.

- Develop the evaluations, observability, and feedback loops needed to understand whether AI features are genuinely useful.

- Work closely with design to create experiences that are fast, intuitive, and polished.

- Talk directly with customers and translate ambiguous needs into simple product decisions.

- Make pragmatic architectural choices that balance speed, quality, maintainability, and performance.

- Improve the systems and engineering practices that help a small team ship reliably at high velocity.

- At Staff level, provide technical direction across projects, raise the engineering bar, and help other engineers make better decisions.

What we’re looking for

- Significant experience building and shipping high-quality, customer-facing software. 5+ years is a useful guide, but the scope and quality of your work matter more than the number.

- Strong TypeScript and React fundamentals, with experience working across the full stack.

- Strong product and technical judgment. You care about what should be built, how it should feel, and whether it actually solves the problem. You can distinguish between problems that need a sophisticated system and problems that need a simple, well-executed solution.

- Experience building with LLMs or other applied AI systems in production.

- An understanding of the challenges behind reliable AI products: evaluation, context, retrieval, model behavior, latency, cost, observability, and failure modes.

Waniwani builds the infrastructure that distributes insurance and banking products through AI assistants. We raised an $8M seed led by Seedcamp and work with large European banks and insurers. Each enterprise deal has to be scoped, architected, and deployed into a regulated environment. This role owns the layer between a signed deal and a live deployment.

The role 

- Customer workshops, discovery, and requirements (35%). Run technical discovery and workshops with each client, and translate their needs into clear, buildable product requirements for our sales, ops, and engineering teams. Flag what we need to build to support a given setup, such as client self-hosting.

- Solution architecture and documentation (35%). Design the end-to-end MCP flow and integration architecture for each client, including hosted versus on-premise scenarios, and produce the technical documentation enterprise clients require (BPI France alone is roughly 50 docs).

- Procurement, security, and delivery oversight (30%). Use our existing compliance library (SOC 2 program, DPAs, prior questionnaire answers) to complete security questionnaires, handle security committees and data-residency questions, and drive procurement to completion. Oversee the MCP deployment itself, which our freelancer network implements.

Across all three, you build the reusable kit that makes this repeatable: scoping templates, architecture patterns, and a procurement answer library.

Objectives 

- 90 days: own scoping and procurement response for active deals, with the reusable kit used on at least one live deal end to end.

- 6 months: run the full signed-to-live pipeline, including architecture decisions and procurement ownership, without founders in the critical path.

- 12 months: a repeatable delivery process with patterns reused across clients, and a case for the first hire under this role.

Requirements 

- You are technically credible: you read code, reason fluently about integrations and the MCP and agent stack, and can scope and oversee a deployment. This is not a hands-on production-coding role; implementation is handled by our freelancer network.

- You are comfortable leading technical conversations with enterprise clients.

- You can drive a security questionnaire or procurement process to completion from existing documentation.

- You have worked in or near regulated industries (finance, insurance) and understand compliance and data residency requirements.

- You work well in ambiguity across sales, ops, and engineering, and ramp into new domains quickly.

- You have an interest in the MCP and agent stack.

- You are open to traveling from time to time across Europe and the US to meet clients.

What this role is not 

- A backend engineering role. You will work with clients most of the week.

- A pure pre-sales role. You own architecture, requirements, and delivery oversight, not only the pitch.

- A slideware role. You need real technical depth, even though you are not writing production code day to day.

Practicalities 

- Remote-first, based in Europe. Expect travel roughly once a month, primarily Paris, London, and Madrid, with US travel around the 6-month mark. Being able to come to Paris occasionally is a plus but not required.

- First hire in this function, working directly with the founders and the engineering team.

Process 

- Intro call with our talent partner.

- 30-minute conversation with Max, our CTO.

- Work sample based on a real client scenario (live session): scope the flow, draft the architecture, and handle a mock procurement Q&A.

- Discussions with Robin, our CEO, Luiza, and members of the tech team.

- Reference checks.

title: Senior iOS Developer - Berlin
description:
About RA

Resident Advisor has been a home for electronic music culture since 2001. Event discovery, ticketing, news and long-form editorial, artist profiles, original films, and a weekly mix series two decades deep. Around 7 million people use the web platform every month, with a wider audience across our apps and other channels. Underneath the platform sits a network of contributors and city managers across dozens of cities, which is how we stay connected to the scenes we cover rather than reporting on them from a distance. RA is 25 years old, independent, B.Corp certified and intent on being indispensable to the artists, promoters and audiences who make this culture.

The role

You'll be a senior engineer on the RA Guide iOS app: shaping how it's built, leading the technical design of larger features, and raising the bar on quality with the Apps lead.

RA Guide is RA's app for browsing events and buying tickets, native on iOS and Android and used by thousands of people every day. We also make RA Scan, a cross-platform app promoters use to scan tickets at the door. You'll join the Apps team: the Apps lead (who also builds on iOS), an Android developer and a product manager, working closely with design and the web teams who build the APIs the app uses.

We release weekly. Native releases can't be rolled back once they're out, so we care about getting each one right: tests, careful review, and watching what happens after release.

Responsibilities

- Lead the technical design of larger features, including the specs that line up iOS and Android on the same APIs
- Own areas of the codebase, and modernise older parts of it safely
- Raise release quality: automated UI tests on native frameworks, crash analysis and monitoring
- Review code and mentor other developers
- Work with the web and platform teams on the APIs the app depends on
- Help shape how the team uses AI in development, and where it shouldn't.

Who we are looking for

- Several years building and releasing iOS apps used at scale
- Deep experience with Swift, app architecture and refactoring code that's already live
- Testing and coding habits for stable app releases
- You make the developers around you better, through review, pairing and clear explanation
- You can explain a technical trade-off to product and design in plain terms

If you meet most of these but not all, we'd still like to hear from you. We'll help you grow into the rest.

Nice to have 

- SwiftUI, reactive programming and GraphQL
- A/B testing, phased rollouts and data tracking
- Monitoring tools such as Datadog
- Android or cross-platform experience
- An interest in electronic music and the scenes RA serves

What we offer you

- Generous annual leave policies aimed at promoting work-life balance.
- Matched pension, or 401k for US staff.
- Comprehensive staff wellbeing initiatives, featuring regular activities and workplace programmes to support mental and physical health. This includes discounted ClassPass memberships and custom-fitted earplugs.
- Company-led social events, team lunches, and discounts on merch.
- Paid annual volunteering allowance, encouraging contributions to community projects and charities you care about.
- A transparent internal company culture committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion (see: https://ra.co/about/diversity ).
- Active involvement in community projects within the electronic music community (see: https://ra.co/about/community ).

More about RA

We are independent and we intend to stay that way. 25 years in, RA answers to the culture it came from rather than to outside stakeholders. That is what enables us to make decisions on a long-term basis.

Our staff, contributors and international teams are not observers. They are part of the scenes we cover, and that is what we hire for. Craft first, and then a genuine stake in this music rather than just a job in it.

RA has been B Corp certified since 2024, which holds us to standards on social and environmental impact we would want to meet regardless of the badge.

We especially welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, abilities, ethnicities, experiences, gender identities, and sexual orientations.

Our values

- Electronic music is art.
- We celebrate the progressive values that underpin electronic music.
- We advocate for a more inclusive and equitable electronic music community.
- We honour the past, present and future of electronic music.
- We use innovation to empower the community.
- We choose honesty over gain and purpose over profit.
- We're always front left.

This role is a full-time based in our Berlin office. Please note: this position requires applicants to be based in Berlin and to work from the office three days per week. The annual salary range for this role is €70,000- €85,000. If you have questions about the role, please contact

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer / SRE – Kubernetes & Hybrid Cloud (m/f/d)
description:
Introduction At a glance 

- Location & work model : Berlin, hybrid 
- Tech stack: Kubernetes on our own servers, Harvester ( KubeVirt ), Argo CD/Flux, Prometheus/Grafana, Longhorn/Ceph 
- Team: A growing SRE team – you report to our CTPO for now and to the Team Lead SRE we're hiring next; two system administrators in Pforzheim run the physical hardware 
- Process: Intro call · take-home task (~2h) · 90-min tech interview with our developers · leadership conversation · meet the team 
- Languages: Fluent English required; German is a plus, not a must 
Why this role is special 

Most SRE jobs today mean clicking around a managed cloud console. This one doesn't. We run our own hardware in Frankfurt and are building a modern private cloud platform on Kubernetes and Harvester – on-prem by default, with elastic burst into the public cloud and the option to go cloud-only later. You won't inherit a finished SRE practice: you'll help define it, side by side with our Berlin development teams – and you won't do it alone, a Team Lead SRE hire is coming next. 

SRE here is an enabling discipline: you build what our developers need to ship reliably, while two system administrators in Pforzheim run the physical hardware. And the impact is direct – our product discovery technology powers more than 2,000 European online shops (Intersport, SPAR, Douglas and more), handling billions of shopper queries a year. When product discovery is slow or down, our customers lose revenue in real time. 

Your first 90 days 

You get to know both products, join the on-call rotation with a buddy, and own your first reliability topic – SLOs for one product, alerting that actually helps at 3 a.m., or automating away a piece of toil. By day 90 you've shipped visible improvements and know where you want to take the platform next.

Your mission - Define and own SLOs, SLIs and error budgets; drive data-informed reliability decisions
- Lead incident response end-to-end: fast detection, clear communication, blameless postmortems – and reduce whole classes of incidents structurally, not case by case
- Eliminate toil through automation and GitOps; evolve our observability (metrics, logs, traces, alerting, runbooks) across two different stacks
- Help build our custom Kubernetes operator (CRDs) that makes stateful search clusters declarative, self-healing and safely upgradable – and roll out the auto-scaling (HPA/VPA, KEDA, cluster auto scaler) today's architecture makes hard
- Plan capacity, performance and cost across on-premises and cloud – including the large-catalogue and peak-season loads our merchants care about – and use AI tools wherever they measurably speed up diagnosis and operations

Your profile Must-haves: 
- Kubernetes in production – built, not just used : you've set up and maintained clusters on your own servers (e.g. kubeadm , RKE2, k3s) and know cluster lifecycle and upgrades – managed-only experience isn't enough for this role 
- Lived SRE practice : SLOs, error budgets, incident management, on-call 
- Hands-on experience with GitOps or comparable infrastructure/deployment automation – experience with Argo CD or Flux is a strong plus 
- Solid observability skills – metrics, logs, traces, alerting that people trust 
- A strong automation instinct – you'd rather fix a problem's cause than repeat its workaround 
- A collaborative, enabling mindset – you see SRE as a service to our developers: you ask what they need, discuss trade-offs openly, and don't fall in love with your own solution 
Nice-to-haves (genuinely optional – we'll teach you the rest): 
- Harvester, KubeVirt , vSphere/ ESXi , OpenStack or similar virtualization/HCI platforms 
- Container storage (Longhorn, Ceph) and datacenter networking (load balancing, ingress, VLAN) 
- Auto-scaling (HPA, VPA, KEDA, cluster auto scaler ) and capacity/cost planning 
- Experience building Kubernetes operators/CRDs 
- German language skills 
Certifications (CKA, CKS) are welcome but no substitute for hands-on experience – in the tech interview we'll ask about what you've actually built and operated. 

You don't tick every box – or your title was never “SRE”? Apply anyway. If you've owned production systems, handled incidents and worked deeply with Kubernetes, we want to hear from you – production experience and engineering mindset matter more to us than titles or buzzwords.

THE JOY OF WORKING WITH US - Impact from day one: Your work directly influences the revenue of leading eCommerce brands across Europe.
- Modern tech stack: Kubernetes, Harvester, GitOps, auto-scaling, and an exciting path toward the cloud – with room to build things right.
- AI-first mindset: We use AI as a real part of our daily work, not as a buzzword.
- Ownership & growth: Clear responsibility, short decision paths, and the opportunity to actively shape your role.
- Flexible work: Hybrid work model three office days per week with a focus on outcomes.
- Strong team: Experienced engineers, an open feedback culture, and an environment where reliability is treated as a real engineering discipline.

Job Location Berlin, Munich, Pforzheim or Stockholm (all Hybrid)

title: Senior Product Manager, Wealth & AI (f/m/d)
description:
What we do At getquin, we're on a mission to empower everyone to build wealth.

Founded in 2020, we started with a simple idea: help people see their entire financial life in one place, so they can make more informed decisions.

Today, getquin has grown into one of the largest wealth platforms globally, already helping over half a million users manage and grow their wealth. Our platform combines analytics, tools and community to make wealth-building accessible for everyone, not just the experts.

After launching in Germany, we've started expanding across Europe, with a focus on growing our user base, building valuable new features and helping even more people take control of their financial future.

If you're excited to help shape the future of personal wealth management, join us. We're just getting started.

What you'll be doing You've built products for investors. You know what a TER actually does to a long-run return, why a user with four brokers has no visbility what they really own, and how differently people behave when the number on screen is their pension rather than their pocket money.

You've probably also hit the ceiling of what a chart can tell someone. Better tables, more filters, another allocation donut. The data was always there; the answer never quite arrived.

We have something nobody else has: a complete, cross-institution picture of a person's wealth. Investments, cash, liabilities and insurance contracts, in one place, for over half a million users. Your work is turning that into features and insights people understand and act on, and the interesting tools for doing that now include AI.

We're looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own that area. You'll work directly with the founders and the product team, alongside engineering and our financial advisory teams. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports, and you'll mentor less experienced product managers on the team.

Own the wealth product area end to end 

- Set the product strategy and roadmap across the picture we give people of their wealth and how we help them optimize it
- Decide what we build on aggregated portfolio data that nobody with a single-broker view could build at all
- Own our efforts to stay on the forefront of digital wealth management services and play your part in disrupting a still very offline industry
- Work the unglamorous, high-leverage problems too: data quality, coverage gaps, missing cost basis, duplicate holdings across connections, ETFs held through more than one broker. A portfolio insight is only as trustworthy as the numbers under it
Turn the data into something users act on 

- Define the insights we surface about someone's portfolio, cash position and risk, and why each one earns a place on their screen
- Own our conversational AI assistant and our AI-driven insights: what they say, what they refuse to say, and how a user knows which is which
- Set the quality bar for anything we tell a user about their money: accuracy targets, human review, guardrails, rollback. Decide when something is good enough to ship and hold that line when the pressure is to ship anyway
Own the numbers 

- Define the metrics for your area: activation, engagement, the insight-to-action funnel, and contribution to subscription conversion and retention
- Run the experiments, including proper A/B testing, read them, and report what didn't work alongside what did
- Live in your own product analytics and write your own queries and reporting, rather than wait for someone to give that to you

What we are looking for You might be a fit if: 

- You've built wealth management, investing or portfolio products. You know the domain properly: instruments, ETFs, costs, allocation, risk, tax drag, and how retail investors actually behave rather than how they should. This is the requirement we're least flexible on
- You've owned a product area end to end against a number you defined yourself, with real experimentation behind it
- You've shipped at least one AI or LLM-based feature to production for real users, and you owned its output quality. 
- You've shipped inside a legal or compliance constraint, and you can reason about where an insight becomes advice. 
- Your product discovery produces evidence, not opinion. You can show us a real research artefact and a decision that changed because of it
- You're fluent in English; German is a plus
- You can work from our Berlin office, and you already have the right to work in Germany
That usually adds up to around five or more years in product, but we care about the evidence, not the year count. If you came to product from engineering, data science, research, design, financial services, or from a Product Owner role, that counts. 

Strong plus if you have: 

- PSD2, open banking or account aggregation experience
- Insurance or brokerage product exposure, which matters as we move into advisory
- Recommendation systems or personalisation at scale
- Subscription and paywall experimentation
- Experience mentoring or coaching other product managers
- Your own portfolio, and opinions about it
If you meet most of this and not all of it, apply. We'd rather read your application than guess.

Work authorisation 

This role requires an existing right to work in Germany. We're not able to sponsor visas or support relocation for this position, so we can only consider candidates who already hold German or EU work authorisation, or who can obtain it independently. We'd rather tell you now than after four conversations.

What the first six months look like 

- Month 1: you know the data model, the aggregation layer and its technology behind it. What our analytics do and don't cover, and understand how AI is already being used and where it. You've written down the three things you think are most wrong with the product today
- Months 2 to 3: a written, agreed area strategy with a prioritised roadmap, a primary metric with a baseline, and, clear metrics that you will be monitoring and optimizing along the way
- Months 3 to 4: the first thing you scoped is live to a user segment, with a read on the primary metric, and with quality measurement behind it if it involves generated output
- Months 5 to 6: two or three shipped iterations with measured results, including the ones that didn't work, a quality bar the team applies without you in the room, and at least one junior product manager who's visibly better at their job because of you
You won't be measured on shipping volume. You'll be measured on whether your area got measurably more useful and more trustworthy.

Why join getquin? Why join getquin? 

We're a fast-growing B2C fintech, and here, your work has real impact. From day one, you'll take ownership of your domain, ship features end-to-end, and help shape the direction of a product used across Europe. We value initiative, ownership and creativity, not layers of process.

Three things that are specifically true of this role:

- Wealth management is ripe for disruption. Following digitalisation waves of banking and brokerage services, we are leading those efforts across the next big topic for private individuals: better understand and optimize your wealth
- The data asset is genuinely rare. Aggregated cross-institution wealth for half a million people, with over +€25bn in connected assets. Trade Republic sees its own platform. N26 sees the current account. Nobody else in Europe sees the whole picture, which means there are product questions you can only answer here
- You'll own the area, not a slice of it. At our size the decisions are yours
Ready to build something meaningful? Then join us at the forefront of making wealth building accessible to everyone.

How we hire 

Five conversations, typically three to four weeks from first call to decision. We tell you where you stand after every step, and we respond within seven days at every stage.

- Recruiter screen, 30 min, video. Role, scope, the salary band, hybrid expectation, notice period, work authorisation. No trick questions
- Hiring manager, 60 min, video. Your product area ownership, the outcome you drove, and your depth in the wealth domain. This is the first real fit conversation, in both directions
- Product case, take home. We give you a real getquin problem on aggregated wealth data and work through it together. We know you already have a job, hence we do not impose an in-person case during working hours
- Cross-functional panel, 2 x 30 min, in our Berlin office. Cover in more depth your case study and deep dive further in your understanding of product metrics and approach to product development. Usually in person in our office.
- Close conversation, 30 min. Team fit, how you like to work, and whatever is still open, including your questions for a founder
Along the last part we will be making reference checks, but only with former employers. Once we have this, we will make you a formal offer. 

The whole loop runs in English. Tell us if you need any adjustment to the process, whether timing, format or accessibility, and we'll make it. You don't need to explain why.

title: Full Stack Product Developer (m/w/d)
description:
Aufgaben  Du willst Technologie gestalten, die direkt etwas bewegt? 

Bei Table.Briefings entwickeln wir digitale Produkte für ein wachsendes Medienunternehmen. Unsere Software hilft dabei, Prozesse effizienter zu machen, neue Geschäftsmodelle zu ermöglichen und unseren Redaktionen den Rücken freizuhalten – damit sie sich auf das konzentrieren können, was sie am besten können: hochwertigen Journalismus!
Als dritter interner Entwickler bzw. dritte interne Entwicklerin übernimmst du eine zentrale Rolle in unserem Tech-Team. Du arbeitest an der gesamten Entwicklungskette: von der ersten Idee über Konzeption und Umsetzung bis zu Deployment, Betrieb und Weiterentwicklung.
Dabei geht es nicht nur darum, Features zu programmieren. Du hilfst uns, die richtigen Probleme zu erkennen, Anforderungen zu schärfen und Lösungen zu entwickeln, die für unser Business, unsere Nutzerinnen und Nutzer und unsere Redaktionen wirklich einen Unterschied machen. 

Deine Aufgaben 

- Du konzipierst, entwickelst und betreust unsere Webanwendungen, APIs und Apps. 
- Du arbeitest an unseren Statamic -basierten Plattformen und entwickelst unser CMS weiter. 
- Du entwickelst neue Funktionen mit unserem bestehenden Tech-Stack und verbesserst bestehende Lösungen kontinuierlich. 
- Du beschäftigst dich mit dem Einsatz und der Optimierung von Large Language Models und Coding Agents – zur Automatisierung interner Prozesse und für neue Produktfeatures. 
- Du entwickelst und integrierst RESTful APIs, zum Beispiel zur Anbindung von Systemen wie ActiveCampaign . 
- Du wirkst bei der Konfiguration, Wartung und Absicherung unserer Linux-Server und Deployment -Prozesse mit. 
- Du übersetzt Anforderungen aus unterschiedlichen Bereichen in klare technische Lösungen. 
- Du bringst Struktur in komplexe oder noch nicht vollständig definierte Aufgaben und sorgst dafür, dass aus Ideen umsetzbare Produkte werden. 
- Du arbeitest eng mit Stakeholdern, Produktverantwortlichen, Redaktion und Geschäftsführung zusammen. 
Unser Tech-Stack - Wir arbeiten unter anderem mit: 

- PHP und Laravel 
- Statamic 
- PostgreSQL 
- Livewire 
- HTML, CSS und JavaScript 
- RESTful APIs 
- Linux-Servern und modernen Deployment -Prozessen 
- Large Language Models und Coding Agents 
Du musst unseren Tech-Stack nicht bereits vollständig beherrschen – wichtiger sind uns dein technisches Verständnis, deine Kommunikationsstärke und deine Fähigkeit, komplexe Anforderungen schnell in gute Lösungen zu übersetzen. Du solltest aber Lust haben, mit unseren Technologien zu arbeiten und dich schnell in neue Systeme und Themen einzuarbeiten. 
Wir suchen keine Person, die jedes Tool schon einmal eingesetzt hat, sondern jemanden, der gute technische Entscheidungen trifft, Zusammenhänge versteht und Verantwortung übernimmt.

Qualifikation - Du hast fundierte Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung und beherrschst mindestens eine relevante Programmiersprache sicher. 
- Du hast idealerweise Erfahrung mit Webanwendungen, APIs und Datenbanken. 
- Du interessierst dich für unseren Tech-Stack und hast Lust, dich in Laravel , Statamic , PostgreSQL und Livewire einzuarbeiten oder darin weiterzuentwickeln. 
- Du verstehst, wie man LLMs und Coding Agents sinnvoll und verantwortungsvoll in der Softwareentwicklung einsetzt – oder möchtest es lernen. 
- Du kennst dich mit Linux-Servern, Deployment und grundlegenden Fragen der IT-Sicherheit aus oder bist bereit, dich in diese Themen einzuarbeiten. 
- Du kannst komplexe Probleme schnell erfassen, priorisieren und in konkrete nächste Schritte übersetzen. 
- Du kommunizierst klar und gerne – auch mit Menschen, die nicht technisch arbeiten. 
- Du kannst unterschiedliche Anforderungen und Perspektiven zusammenbringen und sicher mit Stakeholdern umgehen. 
- Du arbeitest selbstständig, zuverlässig und lösungsorientiert. 
- Du behältst auch dann den Überblick, wenn Anforderungen sich verändern, Informationen zunächst unvollständig sind oder mehrere Themen gleichzeitig auf dem Tisch liegen. 
- Du hast Freude daran, in solchen Situationen Ruhe, Struktur und Verbindlichkeit zu schaffen. 
- Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sind für die Kommunikation im Team und mit unseren Stakeholdern unerlässlich. 
Was uns wichtig ist 

Wir entwickeln nicht zum Selbstzweck. Unser Ziel ist Software, die unmittelbar Wirkung entfaltet: für unser Geschäft, für die Vervielfachung unserer Lizenzen und für unsere Redaktionen, die täglich anspruchsvolle Inhalte produzieren.
Dafür suchen wir eine Persönlichkeit, die Verantwortung übernimmt, Fragen stellt und sich aktiv einbringt. Du solltest dich in einem meinungsstarken, dynamischen Umfeld wohlfühlen, unterschiedliche Perspektiven aushalten und deine eigenen Ideen überzeugend vertreten können. Gleichzeitig ist uns wichtig, dass du pragmatisch bleibst und gemeinsam mit anderen zu guten Lösungen kommst.

Benefits Wir bieten dir: 

- Eine Schlüsselposition in einem innovativen und wachstumsstarken Medienunternehmen 
- Die Möglichkeit, unseren Tech-Stack aktiv mitzugestalten und weiterzuentwickeln 
- Viel Eigenverantwortung und kurze Entscheidungswege 
- Einen vielseitigen Job mit direktem Einfluss auf unser Business und unsere Produkte 
- Eine unbefristete Festanstellung in Teilzeit oder Vollzeit 
- 28 Tage Urlaub 
- Flexibilität bei Arbeitszeit und Arbeitsort > Drei Tage pro Woche in unserem Büro in Berlin-Mitte, zwei Tage im MobileOffice 
- Persönliche und fachliche Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten in einer echten Wachstumskultur 
- Eine offene, freundliche Atmosphäre mit Partnerinnen, Partnern und Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus der ganzen Welt 

Deine Bewerbung 

Wir freuen uns auf deinen Lebenslauf und ein kurzes, persönliches Motivationsschreiben mit maximal 1.000 Zeichen: Warum möchtest du als Full Stack Product Developer (m/w/d) bei Table.Briefings arbeiten? 

Uns interessiert besonders, welche Probleme du gerne löst, wie du mit unterschiedlichen Anforderungen umgehst und was dich daran reizt, Technologie mit konkretem unternehmerischem und redaktionellem Nutzen zu entwickeln.

title: Data Platform Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
We're looking for a Data Platform Engineer (m/f/d) to join our team and help build and operate the data infrastructure that powers Flix's mobility platform.

At FlixTech, our data platform enables teams across the company to process, analyze, and act on large volumes of mobility data. The platform supports critical use cases such as network planning, pricing, operations, and business analytics. You will work on scalable infrastructure that processes millions of daily events and ensures reliable data availability across the organization.

You'll be part of a cross-functional engineering environment collaborating with data analysts, data scientists, and platform engineers. The role focuses on building reliable, scalable data systems and enabling other teams to work efficiently with data.

About the Role 

- Design, build, and maintain scalable data infrastructure running on AWS and Kubernetes

- Develop and operate streaming and data platform components using technologies such as Kafka and Snowflake

- Implement monitoring, alerting, and operational tooling to ensure platform reliability and performance

- Own features end-to-end, including development, testing, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance

- Build and maintain Infrastructure as Code using Terraform and GitLab CI/CD

- Collaborate with data analysts, data scientists, and stakeholders to support data platform use cases

- Contribute to improving platform reliability, automation, and engineering practices

- Participate in on-call rotations to support the stability of the data platform

About You 

- 3+ years of experience building or operating data infrastructure or data platforms

- Hands-on experience with streaming technologies such as Kafka and data warehouses like Snowflake

- Experience with Infrastructure as Code tools (e.g., Terraform) and CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitLab)

- Practical experience with cloud platforms (preferably AWS) and container platforms such as Kubernetes

- Experience with monitoring and observability tools (e.g., Datadog or similar)

- Solid programming skills in Python and interest in writing clean, maintainable code

- Strong collaboration and communication skills when working with technical and business stakeholders

- Fluent in English

Nice to have:

- Experience with advanced SQL or data transformation tools (e.g., dbt)

- Experience with data processing frameworks (e.g., PySpark)

- Knowledge of security and networking concepts relevant for data platforms

We recognize that everyone carries a unique set of valuable skills and experiences. If you think you could have an impact even though you don't meet 100% of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply. We want to hear from you!  

What We Offer 

- Travel perks : 12 free Flix vouchers + 12 discount vouchers for friends & family. 

- Work from (M)Anywhere : Depending on your role, work from another location for up to 60 days per year. 

- Hybrid work model : We are an office-first company, but we offer flexibility to balance work and life. 

- Wellbeing support : Access confidential 1:1 counselling, courses, and stress management for yourself and up to four family members. 

- Learning & Development : Take advantage of language classes, training courses, and expert-led sessions to grow your skills. 

- Mentoring Program : Connect with experienced colleagues to gain insights and accelerate your career. 

To view more local benefits specific to each office location, please check out this link: Locations - Flix Career 

Why Join Flix? 

At Flix, you'll find teams that rally together to overcome challenges and spark creativity. We believe in ownership culture - giving you the freedom to take initiative, make an impact, and shape your own career path. 
As we continue to expand across the globe, you can make a real difference in how we work. 

If you're ready to grow and lead your journey, Flix is the place for you!
